EU and Indonesia sign trade deal

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (328 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The European Union and Indonesia signed a free trade deal on Saturday, describing it as a upcoming chapter in economic relations between the two sides.
  • "This is one of the most ambitious deals the European Union has concluded in Asia," Ursula von der Leyen, president of the European Commission, stated at the signing ceremony on Saturday.
  • "Together, we represent a market of 730 million people," she added.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The European Union and Indonesia signed a free trade deal on Saturday, describing it as a upcoming chapter in economic relations between the two sides.

"This is one of the most ambitious deals the European Union has concluded in Asia," Ursula von der Leyen, president of the European Commission, stated at the signing ceremony on Saturday.

"Together, we represent a market of 730 million people," she added.

The Indonesia-European Union Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) and the additional Investment Protection Agreement (IPA) are designed to reduce trade barriers and attract investment in strategic sectors such as electric vehicles, electronics, and pharmaceuticals.

The agreement comes after almost 10 years of negotiations and is part of a wider series of trade deals by the EU.

The bloc hopes to reduce its reliance on individual economic partners as trade with both China and the US has become more difficult in recent years.

Von der Leyen also stressed the importance of international cooperation, saying that "in a time when others are closing their doors, we keep ours open.".

Sources indicate that the deal sees tariffs on about 98% of EU exports to Indonesia to be done away with. The EU estimates that European companies could save more than €600 million (around $658 million) per year.

Industry observers note that "The benefits for our exporters are concrete and measurable," Indonesian Minister of Economic Affairs Airlangga Hartarto said, hailing a "latest chapter" in economic relations with the EU. He said the deal would benefit his country’s main exports to Europe, including palm oil, footwear and textiles.

Palm oil and deforestation had been major stumbling blocks during the negotiations, and the agreement includes mechanisms for cooperation on regulatory and sustainability issues as well as a dedicated protocol on palm oil to address environmental concerns.

The EU parliament is now expected to greenlight the deal while Indonesian authorities will also complete the ratification process so it can enter into force in 2027.

  • Leading Nashville SC to a record low of 25 goals conceded and tying Tony Meola's record for the most clean sheets in an MLS season with 16, Brian Schwake has taken home Goalkeeper of the Year honors by a landslide, beating out finalists Matt Turner and Roman Bürki.
  • It's astounding that Eduard Lowen is playing soccer, considering what the few years have looked like for him.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that with the MLS Cup playoffs now in full swing, it also means that we are beginning to see who is taking home honors at the end of the season. Nashville SC have already seen Maxwell Woledzi win Defender of the Year and Bran Shwake earn Goalkeeper of the Year honors, and they have potential honorees up and down the awards docket alongside the youngest MVP finalist in league history, Cavan Sullivan, who has taken home young player of the year honors. Antoine Griezmann has also won Newcomer of the Year in only half of a season with Orlando City SC.

Check out the winners and finalists so far:.

Leading Nashville SC to a record low of 25 goals conceded and tying Tony Meola's record for the most clean sheets in an MLS season with 16, Brian Schwake has taken home Goalkeeper of the Year honors by a landslide, beating out finalists Matt Turner and Roman Bürki. In only his first season as the full-time starter for Nashville, Schwake took the reins and didn't look back, also debuting for the U.S. Men's National Team due to his success. He also set club records for wins, penalty kick saves (three), save percentage (78.4%), and goals against average (0.76).

It's astounding that Eduard Lowen is playing soccer, considering what the few years have looked like for him. In March of this year, his wife Ilona died from brain cancer after they managed through her diagnosis, with Lowen taking time off from the game to support her and her family. He returned to MLS play in April, scoring in his first start of the season for St. Louis City SC, but then was traded to San Jose after the World Cup break. During that time with San Jose, he became an important part of their playoff run with one goal and three assists.

Becoming the youngest MVP finalist in league history at only 17, it should come as no surprise that Cavan Sullivan has won Young Player of the Year, beating out the Red Bull Fresh York duo of Julian Hall and Adri Mehmeti. During the World Cup break, Sullivan spent time training with the Union's MLS Next Pro side instead of taking the time off for himself, and the results showed in the second half of the season as he helped lead the Union into a playoff spot. With nine goals and 14 assists (including secondary assists), no teenager has ever been involved in more goals in a season than Sullivan, and it has also led to his first cap with the United States men's national team, where he was able to grab his first goal against Mexico. If this is the tip of the iceberg, we're in for something special, considering that this has been a banner year for young players in MLS, with more minutes being given to teenagers than ever before. The future is in good hands as the kids are leveling up each day.

With Guilherme receiving MVP votes to become a finalist for the award, it was going to take a special performance for someone else to win Newcomer of the Year, and joining Orlando City SC, Antoine Griezmann did just that. Prior to his arrival, this was a team floundering below the playoff line after moving on from manager Oscar Pareja. In only a half-season, he came in and scored 14 goals and assisted eight more as the first player ever to produce 20 goal contributions in only half a season, while turning this team into contenders. It's going to be tough in the playoffs for Griezmann to overcome the defense, but considering what he has already done with the squad, there's no reason why Orlando should be counted out with the Frenchman next to Justin Ellis.

In a recent development, en route to setting a points record with 77 points to win the Supporters' Shield, Nashville SC were also led by a record-setting defense that only let the ball into the back of the net 25 times in an entire campaign. That success was rewarded with all three finalists for Defender of the Year coming from Nashville, but it's their newest signing that took home the award. Joining from Norwegian club Fredrikstad ahead of the season, Woledzi didn't need much time to adjust, appearing in every regular-season match and helping Nashville build from the back to maintain possession. It was a team effort to tie the MLS clean sheet record with 17 during the season, so it's only natural for one of their defenders to get the honors this season.

Mutations in the cancer-associated gene PIK3CA can cause vascular malformations1. These abnormalities can affect people from birth or can be acquired over a person’s lifetime, and they involve veins, capillaries and lymphatic vessels — but rarely arteries2,3. Why are arteries spared? This mystery is investigated by Sabata et al.4 in their paper in Nature.

  • The kit, which combines a white base with black sleeves and neon yellow detailing, was worn for the first time in Saturdayâs 2-0 Bundesliga win over Heidenheim.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Borussia Dortmundâs brand-upcoming away kit for the 2025/26 season has sparked fury among supporters, prompting the club to acknowledge the backlash and vow to respond.

The kit, which combines a white base with black sleeves and neon yellow detailing, was worn for the first time in Saturdayâs 2-0 Bundesliga win over Heidenheim.

In a recent development, but instead of excitement, its debut was met with anger in the stands and online. Fans unfurled banners blasting it as âthe cruelest jersey in the leagueâ while chants of âWe want black and yellow jerseysâ rang out before kick-off, a pointed reminder of the clubâs traditional colours.

Across social media, the reaction was no kinder. Many supporters branded the design a betrayal of Dortmundâs historic identity, with critics arguing it looks more like a training top than a shirt fit for the famous Schwarzgelben.

Club bosses have now pledged to listen.

Recent findings suggest that managing director Carsten Cramer took personal responsibility for the fallout, telling reporters: "The criticism has been received, and we are addressing it. The responsibility lies with me. We won't always be able to please everyone when selecting jerseys.".

Sporting director Sebastian Kehl was more measured, reminding fans that opinions on kit design are always split.

It has been revealed that "I think we have different opinions about jerseys every year," he said. "It will never be the case that a Borussia Dortmund jersey meets with 100 percent approval. Fundamentally, we know which colors represent our city and our club, and that this is reflected in the design of almost all jerseys.".

He added, with a touch of humour: "However, there are also people who want something younger, something fresh, something creative. The new jersey brought BVB three points in Heidenheim. A successful jersey, I'd say. Everything else is a discussion that we as a club consider normal.".

Whether the kit makes another appearance when Dortmund travel to Mainz on September 27 remains to be seen, but if it does, you best believe that Dortmund fans to have something to say about it.

Liverpool Confidential squad audit: The NINE stars who could leave Anfield, the latest on each of their futures and what Reds should do with them

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:00 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 12:08 EST, 26 November 2026.
  • Liverpool's dressing room has felt like a revolving door of uncertainty in the last five years, with constant doubt about certain players’ futures.
  • Even when the team won the Premier League title two seasons ago, there was a never-ending subplot about the futures of Mohamed Salah, Virgil van Dijk and Trent Alexander-Arnold.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:00 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 12:08 EST, 26 November 2026.

Liverpool's dressing room has felt like a revolving door of uncertainty in the last five years, with constant doubt about certain players’ futures.

Even when the team won the Premier League title two seasons ago, there was a never-ending subplot about the futures of Mohamed Salah, Virgil van Dijk and Trent Alexander-Arnold.

Now there is ambiguity over Van Dijk again, plus Alisson, Alexis Mac Allister and others, with the depth of Liverpool's squad still an concern to be addressed.

In this week’s Liverpool Confidential, we take a look at all nine players with uncertain futures, reveal what we are hearing about them, and reach a verdict on what we would do if we were sporting director Julian Ward.

The situation: The 35-year-old club legend's contract runs out at the end of this season, so from January 1 he would be able to sign a pre-contract with an overseas club to join them in the summer.

Owners Fenway Sports Group have a long-standing unwritten policy not to offer big deals to players over the age of 30, which led to the likes of Gini Wijnaldum and Andy Robertson leaving on free transfers. But they broke this rule two years ago to offer Van Dijk a new deal. Will they do it again?

Liverpool's owners FSG broke their rule on offering 30-somethings big deals two years ago to tie down Virgil van Dijk. They should do it again.

What we’re hearing: Van Dijk would be more than open to staying. Sources in Italy say AC Milan have approached him over moving there – but whether he would want to is a completely different story.

In a recent development, van Dijk is yet to be offered a newly introduced deal at Liverpool but this is not a reason for fans to panic. They always bide their time with these things.

Liverpool are carefully managing Van Dijk’s workload for the first time, as evidenced by him being a substitute in Bruges this week. The squad have had a day off on Thursday ahead of returning to training on Friday for the Merseyside derby.

Our verdict: There is a narrative that Van Dijk is starting to show his age. Maybe he is not quite at the extraordinarily high level he maintained in previous years but the skipper is still integral to everything the Reds do. If the two parties can agree on a one-year extension, it would suit everyone. But the Reds must also prepare for life without the formidable Dutchman, whenever that actually happens.

In a recent development, the situation: See above. Alisson is also out of contract at the end of the season after the club triggered a one-year extension last summer.

What we’re hearing: The Brazilian wants to stay and is in talks to do so. There are murmurs that he could ask for a major financial package.

Recent findings suggest that our verdict: Alisson is still in the top three goalkeepers in the Premier League. Like Van Dijk, a short extension might suit everyone.

In a recent development, liverpool are well stocked in the goalkeeper department, with the club believing Giorgi Mamardashvili is better than he has shown so far. They will soon welcome Belgian 18-year-old Lucca Brughmans, who is rated as one of the best up-and-coming keepers in the game.

But are they better than Alisson right now? No.

Alisson wants to stay and remains one of the top three goalkeepers in the Premier League.

The situation: The Argentine has publicly declared he feels let down by the club after he was informed they would not yet extend his contract, and the 27-year-old's deal also runs out at the end of next season.

What we’re hearing: His father and agent Carlos Mac Allister is expecting to hold talks with Liverpool in the coming weeks to set out his demands and may reach a compromise.

It has been revealed that our verdict: Mac Allister has been Liverpool’s best midfielder this season. He has been so good, in fact, that the club should rethink their stance, which they may do with Ward now installed as sporting director.

But there are still 18 months until his deal expires. What if his form falls off a cliff again as it did last season? No one was desperate for a upcoming deal then. Liverpool should bide their time.

Alexis Mac Allister has been Liverpool’s best midfielder this season and, as it stands, deserves a new contract. But why would Liverpool rush into a decision?

The situation: Out of contract in the summer after what will be 12 years at the club.

In a recent development, what we’re hearing: Gomez is still enjoying life at Liverpool despite not being a regular starter. He will turn 30 in the summer so it is hard to see him being handed a newly introduced deal.

Our verdict: The defender is loved by all at the club as the longest-serving player and there is a sadness that injuries have held his career back to a degree. But it feels like this summer would be the right time to move on.

He came close in summer 2024 when he was left out of the first matchday squad of the Arne Slot era, and again in 2025 when Marc Guehi was inches away from signing for Liverpool.

It feels like next summer is the right time for Joe Gomez to move on after over a decade at the club.

The situation: Out of contract in the summer after returning from an unsuccessful loan at Roma last season.

What we’re hearing: You don't need to be a mind-reader to know what the recruitment team are thinking here: Liverpool’s full back department is the weakest area of the squad, especially at left back with neither Tsimikas nor Milos Kerkez impressing this season.

Recent findings suggest that our verdict: Tsimikas seems a well-liked member of the dressing room and will always be remembered for significant moments such as his winning penalty in the 2022 FA Cup final shootout – but the Greek international falls short of Liverpool’s level. A new left back must be on the shopping list.

Kostas Tsimikas seems a well-liked member of the dressing room and will always be remembered for significant moments, but the Greek international falls short of Liverpool’s level.

The situation: The Dutch wing-back has not hit the required level on a consistent basis since joining Liverpool from Bayer Leverkusen for £29.5million last year.

What we’re hearing: There have been reports linking him with a move to Saudi Arabia, but Frimpong has just returned from another injury lay-off and is determined to settle at Liverpool and impress Iraola, who likes attack-minded full backs.

Our verdict: Give him until the end of the season at least. There were glimpses of form last season over the Christmas period. Frimpong does not seem to fit the current system but, given his injuries, he has never really had a chance to prove people wrong.

Jeremie Frimpong is determined to settle at Liverpool and impress Andoni Iraola, who likes attack-minded full backs.

The situation: On loan from Barcelona but Liverpool have an option to sign the 27-year-old Uruguayan for around £47m.

In a recent development, what we’re hearing: No decisions are being made just yet but Liverpool are delighted with the impact made by fan favourite Araujo, and he is loving life in England. Liverpool retain the right to renegotiate and pay less than the pre-agreed fee.

Our verdict: Araujo's leadership, experience and versatility are all huge bonuses. He has been outstanding at both right back and centre half, and it seems like an obvious decision to make the move permanent. Put the money on the table.

Liverpool are delighted with the impact made by fan favourite Ronald Araujo, and he is loving life in England.

The situation: The 33-year-old has not played a single minute under Andoni Iraola, and it is now nine months since his last Liverpool appearance – in a 1-0 win at Sunderland in February. He was excluded from the Champions League squad for the group phase.

What we’re hearing: Endo has never kicked up a fuss but will be keen for game time at this point of his career.

Our verdict: The Japan captain signed as a stop-gap in 2023 and he played an underrated role in the title triumph as a substitute that helped see out games. He played on through injury in that match at Sunderland last season – his only league start of the campaign – and should be given a warm farewell, though a January exit suits everyone.

Wataru Endo has never kicked up a fuss but will be keen for game time at this point of his career.

Federico Chiesa has rarely been fit while at Liverpool and it feels like it is in everyone’s best interests for the Italian to move on.

The situation: The 51-cap Italy winger is not in Liverpool’s Champions League squad and young players like Lewis Koumas and Jayden Danns are ahead of him in the pecking order. The 29-year-old has had just two minutes of competitive action this season.

What we’re hearing: There is a constant background noise of ‘Italian clubs are circling for Chiesa’. An exit seems likely in January, though Chiesa has come close to leaving several times before now and not done so.

It has been revealed that our verdict: Chiesa and Liverpool has just not worked out, despite the Italian becoming a bit of a cult hero last year thanks to some late winners off the bench. He has rarely been fully fit and it feels like it is in everyone’s best interests for the Italian to move on.

    Nicolò Tresoldi: Why 2027 could change everything with a likely transfer and a career-defining decision ahead

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (753 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, there is a upcoming talent in Europe who will make his name in the near future, and that's Nicolò Tresoldi.
    • Industry observers note that when Tresoldi, the son of a former Serie A player, scored the hat-trick against Inter at San Siro, all the headlines were about his childhood and his love for AC Milan, the Nerazzurri's biggest rival, who, according to reports, are also in talks to potentially sign him in the future.
    • Nicolò Tresoldi silences the San Siro 🤫Club Brugge stun Inter 🥶 pic.twitter.com/D8TIEn6b9C.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, there is a upcoming talent in Europe who will make his name in the near future, and that's Nicolò Tresoldi. The 22-year-old is presently playing for Club Brugge and on October 13 scored three goals at San Siro against Inter, showing the world he's ready for the next step in his career. 2027 will be a pivotal year in Tresoldi's career, not only because he could be on the verge of a move to a bigger European club, but also because he may have to make a definitive decision about his international future. With Germany, Italy and Argentina all potentially in the picture, choosing which national team to represent could prove just as significant as his next club move.

    Industry observers note that when Tresoldi, the son of a former Serie A player, scored the hat-trick against Inter at San Siro, all the headlines were about his childhood and his love for AC Milan, the Nerazzurri's biggest rival, who, according to reports, are also in talks to potentially sign him in the future. But just how special is Tresoldi, and which European giants could be in the running to sign him in 2027?

    Nicolò Tresoldi silences the San Siro 🤫Club Brugge stun Inter 🥶 pic.twitter.com/D8TIEn6b9C.

    According to recent reports, tresoldi was born in Cagliari, Sardinia, in 2004, during the summer months when his family would regularly spend time on the island. His connection to Sardinia stemmed from his maternal grandfather, who worked there as a golf instructor. Thanks to this family connection, they had a house on the island and would spend part of their summers there, but because of his mother's job, he moved with his family to Hannover in 2017, when he was 13.

    Tresoldi, who until then had played tennis more regularly, decided to start his soccer career in the Hannover academy, where he debuted with the second team before making his first-team debut in 2022. He immediately drew interest from multiple European clubs, and in the summer of 2025 he joined Club Brugge in Belgium, his first major move as a professional soccer player. In his first season at the club, he scored 23 goals in 58 games, including four in the Champions League's league phase, and he has started his second season even better, with 15 goals in all competitions so far, including that unforgettable hat-trick against Inter in Milan.

    Next year will also be the year he makes a final decision about which national team he wants to represent. Tresoldi is eligible for Germany, Italy and Argentina. In 2023, he decided to join the German U21 team, and he now intends to see out the entire cycle through the 2027 U21 European Championship, which will take place in the summer. Until then, he won't make a final decision, but both Italy coach Roberto Mancini and Germany coach Jürgen Klopp have expressed interest in calling him up.

    Speaking on the topic and about Tresoldi's future, Klopp said: "It doesn't mean that he has made a decision against Germany or Italy. We don't want to put any pressure on the players. It's a sensitive matter, and we will respect whatever decision he makes, without rushing him." Mancini, on the other hand, seemed more optimistic about him choosing Italy: "I've spoken to Tresoldi myself. He needs to feel that he wants to represent our national team. Given that he was born in Italy and has an Italian father, I believe there is a possibility. We hope he makes the right choice; he knows how much he would mean to us." Argentina can also hope to call him up, as his mother is from there, and he could be included in Lionel Scaloni's squad. However, Italy and Germany are his most likely choices.

    Before that, he will also be the subject of transfer rumors starting in the early months of the fresh year, as many top European clubs are looking for a new striker. AC Milan have to be on that list, as the Rossoneri will likely sign a new striker to play alongside Gonçalo Ramos, even though Club Brugge reportedly value him at around $50 million. At the same time, we need to monitor what Bayern Munich do in the January transfer window, as Harry Kane's injury might force the German side to change strategy in the short term. For sure, 2027 will be the year of Tresoldi, as he now focuses his attention on two moves that will shape his future.

    💡 Key Takeaways

    • After Pep Guardiola led the Citizens to 20 trophies in a decade-long tenure, Manchester City turned to Maresca to take charge of the club, with the former Leicester City and Chelsea boss having worked at the Etihad as both the under-23s manager and as one of Guardiola's assistants in the 2022/23 Treble-winning campaign.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Manchester City are considering the future of manager Enzo Maresca, just 19 games into the Italian's stint.

    After Pep Guardiola led the Citizens to 20 trophies in a decade-long tenure, Manchester City turned to Maresca to take charge of the club, with the former Leicester City and Chelsea boss having worked at the Etihad as both the under-23s manager and as one of Guardiola's assistants in the 2022/23 Treble-winning campaign.

    But with uncertainty shrouding the club – following an independent commission finding City guilty of over 100 breaches of serious financial rules across a nine-year period – things may be about to become even more unstable, should the six-time Premier League champions pull the trigger on their manager already.

    Maresca started fantastically after taking over from his former mentor, winning his first seven Premier League games – including a defiant 3-0 thumping of Liverpool at Anfield following the news that City had been found guilty and were facing Premier League sanctions.

    But the Eastlands outfit went on to lose the following three games in the league, drew against Fulham at the weekend, and had to rely on a late Rayan Cherki equaliser against Napoli last night in order to scrape a point in the Champions League.

    Fichajes in Spain are reporting that Maresca “will be fighting for his job” if he doesn't beat Arsenal this weekend, with the Gunners having already outclassed his side 3-0 in the Community Shield earlier this season.

    A defeat at the Emirates Stadium would widen the gap between the pair to a seemingly unassailable nine points, with Liverpool and surprise package Brighton & Hove Albion shaping up to be the champions' biggest threats in completing back-to-back league championships for the first time in almost a century.

    How to become a football referee

    📅 01 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1301 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Honestly, for me it's one of the most rewarding things I've probably ever done.
    • Louise Thompson, women's referee pathway officer for the Irish Football Association, international FIFA referee, and PremierLeague referee in Northern Ireland.
    • Looking after female referees within Northern Ireland, trying to recruit, retain and give them experience within their games to pushthrough into top level refereeing.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Honestly, for me it's one of the most rewarding things I've probably ever done. You find so much more out about yourself that you probably never knew.

    Who are you and what is your job role?

    Louise Thompson, women's referee pathway officer for the Irish Football Association, international FIFA referee, and PremierLeague referee in Northern Ireland.

    What does a women's referee pathway officer do?

    Looking after female referees within Northern Ireland, trying to recruit, retain and give them experience within their games to pushthrough into top level refereeing.

    What kind of training do you give to aspiring referees?

    So from going through recruitment courses first of all, and then we do the beginners course with referees, just giving them all of the Laws of the Game knowledge, then we will also do a practical part of that course where they go onto the pitch and we'll go through scenarios, positioning, things around free kick management for example, other set pieces likecorners, penalty setup, what you do as a referee day to day, even pre match stuff as well, so when you arrive at the grounds, how you check the pitch, check all the equipment is there, how you would interact with players, coaches and then just again, maybe createlike a role play sort of environment so that they know that they're not going totally blind into that sort of situation.

    Have you always been passionate about football?

    Football was a passion of mine, even when I was younger, primary school age, we just didn't have very many female teams, so it normally meant playing with the boys and the boys teams and stuff up until I was about 14, which was the minimum age here you can join senior ladies football team, which is what I did, and played there for 14 years at a club here locally, including up until the Women's Premiership, so it was great to be involved in football, but I always loved watching football, playing football, anything to do with football, I was always there and interested.

    How did you go from playing football to being a referee?

    Sources indicate that becoming a referee for me sort of happened by chance to be honest. It was during a game, one time I got an injury, quite a bad injury to my knee and then I had seen luckily that the referee course was being advertised. So I signed up for it, but I also signed up for a coaching course pretty much at the same time, maybe about six weeks apart. I wasnât really sure which role I wanted to follow, but over that winter I had been pushed into refereeing a wee bit and noted sure, why not, Iâll give it a go, it'd be a bit of extra fitness before my season restarts, and then just fell in love with it from there and never looked back.

    What subjects did you study at school and university?

    Coming through school I always picked PE, so I did my GCSE PE and then I also did A-level PE and then when I went onto university,I had the sport and exercise science as well within that, so I think it gives you a good understanding of obviously how your body works, and your initiative and training, stuff like that as well so you know when you're working nutrition wise, things that you need to know,especially as you reach the top level, just to make sure that you're getting the most out of your body.

    What are your top tips for becoming a referee?

    In a recent development, I would say definitely give it a try for sure. You never know until you do it. I think even when I was a player, I probably never imaginedthat I would be a referee and that I would even achieve and have experienced what Iâve been able to experience. So you never knowuntil you give it a go, but it's also about probably pushing yourself out of your comfort zone, being comfortable with being uncomfortable in situations like that. It's maybe not always as bad as it probably seems it's going to be. There's probably a lot more stigma around being a referee - who wants to be a referee? - but honestly for me, it's one of the most rewarding things I've probably ever done.

    According to recent reports, with a lifelong love of football, Louise Thompson followed her passion for the game, first as a player and now as a referee. As well as refereeing Fifa and NIFL Premiership matches, she also works for the Irish Football Association as the women's referee pathway officer, recruiting and developing up-and-coming female refs.

    Louise Thompson on refereeing the Women's Irish Cup final.

    If you're interested in becoming a referee, it's something you can get involved with from a young age through local referee courses. The minimum age to become a qualified referee varies depending on where in the UK you live:.

    According to recent reports, in her role as a women's referee pathway officer, Louise oversees new referees right from the initial recruitment courses stage: "We then do the beginners' course with referees, giving them all of the Laws of the Game knowledge," she notes. "We also do a hands-on part of that course where they go onto the pitch and we go through different scenariosâ¦ exactly what you do as a referee, and day-to-day practical stuff as wellâ¦ The idea is to give them all the basics and fundamentals before they go into a game so that they're prepared.".

    In a recent development, all four UK nations have established pathways for referee development and progression. Starting out at grassroots level, it's possible to progress all the way to Fifa!

    In a recent development, louise's first games were youth games: "I still remember my first game to this day," she notes. "It was an under-13 game, and I was definitely the most nervous person on the pitch." She explains: "Over time, you'll get mentors who will come and watch you, give you advice, give you feedback" which will help you to progress to higher levels of the game.

    Recent findings suggest that as well as PE, Louise has found that languages are really helpful in this line of work, "especially when you're dealing with a lot of international games and people coming along," she says. "If you can learn some languages, it's very, very useful.".

    You could get into this role by training with a professional body.

    Sources: National Careers Service, GOV.UK, FA, IFA, SFA, and FAW.

    💡 Key Takeaways

    • The incident happened a few hours after a drone attack left a Russian cargo ship ablaze in the Gulf of Finland, the easternmost part of the Baltic Sea.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A Russian helicopter is suspected of violating Finnish airspace, the Nordic country's Ministry of Defense said Saturday.

    The incident happened a few hours after a drone attack left a Russian cargo ship ablaze in the Gulf of Finland, the easternmost part of the Baltic Sea.

    Recent findings suggest that according to Finland's Defense Ministry, the incursion happened at 12:34 p.m. local time (10:34 UTC/GMT) off the town of Loviisa, on the southern coast.

    "This alleged airspace violation may be linked to rescue or surveillance operations carried out by Finland following damage sustained by a cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland," public broadcaster YLE cited Defense Minister Antti Hakkanen as saying.

    The ministry added the helicopter could have penetrated up to 4.1 kilometers (2.5 miles) into Finnish territory.

    Earlier Saturday, Finland — one of NATO's newest members — noted a Russian cargo ship heading for Russia's Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad caught fire after being struck by drones in the Gulf of Finland.

    The Finnish military said the Sparta II was damaged ⁠west ⁠of Russia's Gogland island, about 40 kilometers (25 miles) from Finland's coast, and later drifted into Finnish territorial waters.

    Finnish ‌Border ​Guard Commander Ilja Iljin later told YLE that the vessel, which is known to have links to the Russian military, was struck by Ukrainian  drones while in Russian waters.

    "At the moment, ​there is no confirmed information ⁠about ​what cargo ​is on board, ​but it ‌cannot be ruled out ​that ⁠there is military materiel on ⁠board," ​Iljin said.

    The ship is on a US sanctions list, according to a search of the Open Sanctions website.

    The Border Guard later stated the crew of the Sparta II was evacuating into a life raft and rescue boat.

    "The [Ukraine] war is spilling over into our neighbouring areas," wrote Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo on X.

    Ukraine has the right to fight against the aggressor," he added.

    The Finnish government has put temporary curbs on aviation and maritime traffic in the eastern Gulf of Finland.

    The Defense Ministry remarked Finland had informed its allies about the incident.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that LONDON -- To lose one elegantly-earned lead, Mr. Arteta, may be regarded as a misfortune; to lose two looks like carelessness. Three days after frittering away their lead at Newcastle, Arsenal repeated in the Champions League, as Borussia Dortmund became the first team to stop Mikel Arteta's side from winning a league phase game at the Emirates Stadium.

    According to recent reports, the real impact of two points dropped tonight probably won't become clear until February and the draw for the last 16. A year ago, topping the league table set Arsenal on a favorable path to the Champions League final. There are, of course, no guarantees that they would not get that as a lower seed but a repeat finish in the top two looks unlikely, with Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain both in possession of 100% records.

    Of more immediate concern for Arteta, who was unstinting in his praise of Arsenal's "brilliant performance", is that this team's very good football is not enough to overwhelm their opposition. It is worth noting, at this early juncture, that this team did position itself to potentially overwhelm the German league leaders. As is so often the case with the Gunners, we're assessing them against standards that would be considered unreasonable for 99% of teams. Usually, when you put up 2.2 xG on Borussia Dortmund and give up 0.9, you can be as pleased with your side as Arteta was in public. In private, you can rest assured that he will be as detail-obsessed as this column in attempting to explain why such sustained spells of excellence still end in a share of the points.

    It has been revealed that as at St. James' Park on Saturday night, for 45 minutes here, Arsenal were delicious, a true smorgasbord of footballing delights. Piero Hincapie popping up as an additional center forward, Christos Tzolis gliding off the left, Declan Rice barnstorming from third center back to second attacking midfielder in the space of a single pressing trigger.

    Borussia Dortmund arrived in north London tied with their hosts for the fewest goals conceded in Europe's top five leagues. Niko Kovac's back five, with three robust midfielders ahead of them, looked like it should be enough to stifle the Gunners. Instead, they were overwhelmed, pulled here and there in their attempts to track position-lite red shirts.

    Industry observers note that arsenal's excellence got the goal it deserved, a larruping strike from Viktor Gyokeres that moved one way, then the other, with such extravagance you rather wondered if the Australian cricket team had given the ball a going over beforehand. Nico Schlotterbeck seemed convinced he'd got an edge on it. Gregor Kobel looked dumbfounded. Even Gyokeres' belated donning of the Bane mask suggested he thought there had been some external force aiding him. Not so. You just hit it that well, Viktor.

    From there, Arsenal had all they needed to wrap this game up in style. Their press constricted the game into the spaces where Martin Odegaard could excel. Noni Madueke was even more menacing, a player who seems to have unlocked himself in little over a month. They kept getting into the final third. They kept getting shots, too, 14 of them before the half was out. The problem was how bad those shots were. A baker's dozen and one spare and Arsenal couldn't put up a full expected goal before the break.

    Industry observers note that too often, moves ended prematurely because someone in red fancied taking a swing from range. Eight of their first-half shots were from outside the box. Gyokeres tried a few heat checks; come the final whistle, he was as cold as the north London night. Declan Rice has evidently read Arteta saying that he should try more shots from range. The ones from outside the box, one of which really brought the oohs as it flew over the bar, weren't even his worst. Not squaring for Madueke in the first half or Gyokeres in the second really was a spurning of prime opportunities.

    Recent findings suggest that if this rush to shoot from range were a one-off, you could frame it as Arteta did in his post-match press conference, "a variation in relation to the opponent, the situation that you have". And yet Arsenal have been trying from range more frequently this season, from fewer than four shots per game in 2025-26 to nearly five this term, a 23% increase in shot volume from range. Against Newcastle, the proportions were lower but twice in an excellent 45 minutes, they shot when they could have worked the ball into a better spot. Arteta has spoken about unlocking the long-range potential of his team. Those who know his thinking often frame his obsession with adding "gamechangers" to his roster in terms of players who can beat a man and strike one from deep.

    They still take a lower proportion of efforts from outside the box than most teams in Europe's top five leagues but most teams in Europe's top five leagues don't employ Martin Odegaard. For now, the sample size and the variation might be so small as to be explained through happenstance or circumstances rather than design. Bukayo Saka's injury has removed one of Arsenal's primary penalty-box threats from this team. His replacement, Madueke, is still honing his shot profile, if we're being generous.

    There is also value to a team that faces so many low blocks proving themselves to be willing to strike from range. Fail to close down an Eberechi Eze and you might well be picking the ball out of your net soon after. Get those defenders moving out of position to close down the shot and an angle to a better opening might present itself.

    It is a hard balance to strike. Tonight, Arsenal did not quite manage it: prime positions turned into subprime shots because trigger fingers got itchy.

    A driving run from Joane Gadou took him away from Christos Tzolis, as the midfield busied themselves with other matters. Maximilian Beier received the ball in the box and smartly turned away from Gabriel before drilling low past Kepa Arrizabalaga. Even a defense as excellent as Arsenal's can't keep your average Premier League or Champions League opponent from clicking once. The levels are just too high.

    It has been revealed that an upswing in pressure in the final 35 minutes brought enough moments to leave Arteta baffled. "There is an element of luck here because how in hell some of the goals they haven't gone in, I don't know. Some of the days last year we hit somebody and it was an own goal.

    "Quality sometimes [is missing], or [there is a] rush, or [a need] to have a bit of composure, or to read the next pass a little bit better; the execution can be better, but everything that is in between that, I think was really, really good.".

    He is not wrong. It just seems even more careless to let two points slip away because they could not quell their shot-first instincts.

    The Kith x adidas Football Fall 2025 collection is available from September 19 via Kith's online and in-person stores.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Thomas Tuchel may not have planned it this way, but in one night he gave us all the rich history of the England team at once: some glorious attacking football, some self-sabotage defending, a red card, a late siege and a fight.

    Recent findings suggest that this was the beguiling story of Spain 2 England 3, an evening that began with the world champions parading the World Cup trophy and ended with 10 Englishmen defending a lead with their last breath. England beat the world champions in Madrid, and for more than 30 minutes including injury time they did so with 10 men, Dan Burn heading the last ball out as per the tradition of a defensive rearguard action.

    This was the game that had it all: including a substitute, in Djed Spence, who had already picked up a yellow card on the bench before he came on. It was a coming-of-age performance in goal for James Trafford. So too for Ben White, the 2022 World Cup departee who scored the third and lunged with astonishing effect in the 84th minute to block a Nico Williams shot.

    In a recent development, trafford again! 👊🏻 An excellent double save from the Leeds United keeper 🙌 https://t.co/L27oQFQO1J.

    This was a performance good enough to win a World Cup final, never mind Nations League Group A3 – just a shame England neglected to get to that World Cup final in the summer. The fight in question was at half-time as the players came off and White and Fabián Ruiz first tangled and others dived in.

    There was so much to admire. England began the night testing Spain’s first-phase passing to breaking point. They began the second half counter-attacking Spain for two goals from Ezri Konsa and White. Then after Elliot Anderson’s red card, this was a different England. With Trafford in inspired form, they held off the relentless Spain for long enough.

    It has been revealed that harry Kane scored his 93rd England goal from the spot and was replaced before the end so that Myles Lewis-Skelly’s energy could give the midfield one more lease of life. By the end, the excitement meant that Kane was unable to take his seat on the bench, and he stood alongside Tuchel in the technical area, cajoling and advising.

    England have beaten Spain on Spanish territory in recent times, but it was the nature of this performance, its many qualities when the moment required them, that made it so significant. This was the end of a 43-game unbeaten streak for the European and world champions, and it was ended by an England team in their best form in recent years.

    It has been revealed that only three who started this game – Kane, Jude Bellingham and Declan Rice – started the final of Euro 2024, lost to Spain. Tuchel’s pool of talent is deeper than it was for his predecessor but there is also a greater maturity to the way they play. The England manager called it the greatest performance of almost two years in charge “given the circumstances… who we play, where we play” and as ever for England just slightly too late.

    The defeat by Argentina in the semi-final in Atlanta just stings that little bit more when one considers the craft and resilience England demonstrated on this night. They were under the hammer after Anderson threw an arm over the shoulder of Lamine Yamal and was dismissed before Mikel Oyarzabal converted the penalty that followed. “Thirty minutes against Spain in Spain feels like three hours,” Tuchel remarked, although Spain had a long way back after the blitzing they took at times in the first hour.

    They all had their moments. Anthony Gordon had a strong first half. Morgan Rogers was central to the two goals England scored in the 10 minutes after the break. Anderson demonstrated that he is one of the best midfielders in the world in the hour before his red card. Spain were without Rodri and in his absence his Manchester City successor was in control.

    In a recent development, tuchel encouraged his players to mount a ferocious press against the best first-phase passing team in the world. Brave, but it worked beautifully and for an absorbing opening 10 minutes, Spain looked all at sea. Such was the pressure, the Spain goalkeeper Unai Simón abandoned the usual build-up strategy and released his goal-kicks to the halfway line.

    According to recent reports, even when Spain finally found their rhythm at the mid-point of the first half, England adapted. It took them a while to manage the discomfort of being denied the ball, and the familiar rapid incursions and switches of play. The counter-attacking switch from the early period pressing Spain in their own area yielded the penalty from which Kane scored the first.

    Industry News: What to watch in UEFA Champions League: Manchester United face defensive crisis in tough visit to Sporting

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, another week of Champions League football comes to a close on Wednesday night as plenty of teams on the top-eight or even top-24 bubble find themselves with work to do.
    • Industry observers note that do Manchester United have such lofty aspirations?
    • If there was a silver lining to the very dark clouds over Manchester United on Sunday, it would have been that there is at least plenty of time to cure what ails them in the Premier League.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, another week of Champions League football comes to a close on Wednesday night as plenty of teams on the top-eight or even top-24 bubble find themselves with work to do. A shock loss to Club Brugge means that there is pressure on Inter as they face Stuttgart at the San Siro; certainly, if they are to take up a top-eight berth, this is a game they are going to have to win.

    Industry observers note that do Manchester United have such lofty aspirations? It is with the Red Devils we start, and no wonder, given their trying run of form lately. That they do have as many wins as defeats from their first four games is almost a surprise, but a difficult fixture list demonstrates no sign of easing for Mauricio Pochettino as his side faces Sporting in Lisbon tonight.

    If there was a silver lining to the very dark clouds over Manchester United on Sunday, it would have been that there is at least plenty of time to cure what ails them in the Premier League. A point from safety is a disastrous place for such an august team to be at any point in the domestic season, but when there is more than 70% of it left to play, at least the danger is not yet cataclysmic. As for the Champions League, well, United are drifting nearer to that point.

    With half their games played, they have six points. Not bad, you would have to say, good enough for 17th place in the league phase. The trouble is that their remaining four games all look difficult indeed: RB Leipzig and Bayern Munich at Old Trafford either side of Christmas, then a trip to a Villarreal outfit that should have plenty to play for on the final day. Tonight's visit to Sporting might be as good a shot at three points as Pochettino gets, and the Portuguese giants have three wins from four. He will not want to be trying to accrue four-plus points in three games.

    It's all feeling very high stakes in league and Europe, the sort of moment when clear heads are needed. Not one for doom and gloom, or for Kobbie Mainoo to tell United's in-house channel "we're at the lowest we've ever been and no one's coming to save us." Then again, he's not wrong.

    Already this club looks like it's doom-spiraling. It's on Pochettino to fix that. His first task will surely be to rustle up a defensive quartet who at least don't magnify each other's flaws. Does Matthijs de Ligt need time out to find the sharpness he so lacked against Liverpool? Can anyone fill in at left back? Diogo Dalot, still, really? Their organization will be tested against a Sporting side that attacks quickly and centrally, qualities that should terrify a backline that will likely be shielded by the slow-moving Mainoo and Youri Tielemans.

    According to recent reports, sporting always score, their 22-game streak of goals in the group stage and league phase a record for a Portuguese club. Right now it looks like United are doomed to forever concede. This could get dicey.

    In spite of what you might assume about Italian clubs, Inter's success at home and on the continent has not always been underlaid with defensive excellence. Certainly, there have been some memorable individual displays, none more so than Yann Sommer standing tall against the Barcelona onslaught, but great defense tends not to be about one player doing the spectacular over and over. After all, sometimes excellence is required because of mistakes elsewhere.

    And right now mistakes are plaguing Inter across the field. Their 12 Serie A games have seen the concession of 17 goals, two in the final 10 minutes at Atalanta turning what might have been a valuable 4-2 win on the road into a chastening draw. It's the same story in the Champions League, where there have been a competition-high four errors leading to goals and another three leading to shots. Those sorts of numbers may not be very predictive, but in this case they feel indicative of a defense that has taken a step down from a level that wasn't that high to begin with.

    Some of that problem lies with recruitment. It might have been time to move on from Sommer, but Josep Martinez has not proven himself to have been the ready-made replacement in the wings he might have been. Francesco Acerbi and Stefan de Vrij were similarly long in the tooth, and there was an argument for swapping out experience for experience in the form of ex-Manchester City duo Manuel Akanji and John Stones. The glitch when you keep going for old guys, though, is that some of them are on the downslope (Akanji) and others can't stay fit (Stones). Being a bit too old might be an issue in midfield too.

    According to recent reports, these failings are being particularly exposed in the Champions League, where Club Brugge, Real Madrid and even Shakhtar Donetsk have ended up with good shot volume and expected goals. Domestically, Inter allow a solid 1.1 non-penalty expected goals (npxG) per game, but maybe that says more about the field in Serie A. Or maybe there's just a lot of air in four Champions League games in which 7.6 npxG has been allowed.

    According to recent reports, it might be true that, as the graphic indicates, Inter's defense has stabilized a bit of late after a bad start to the season, although it probably did not feel like that when Milan were scoring three goals off 0.62 xG. It also helps no end when the attack is firing, Francesco Pio Esposito giving Cristian Chivu every manager's favorite sort of headache. However, against a Stuttgart side that can test the best defenses -- 1.96 npxG per Bundesliga game, 2.09 in the Champions League -- that defense is going to have to get its house in order.

    Has it finally clicked for Florian Wirtz? Well, maybe. The 23-year-old leads the Premier League in chances created, trails only Declan Rice for assists provided, and is one of only five players with over two expected assists from open play this season. All that, and he ranks in the top 20 for shots and in the 91st percentile for npxG. At 11 games, it might be worth considering a few caveats. Nineteen of his 33 chances created came against Brentford and Manchester United. In the match against the former, there were an awful lot of sideways passes that resulted in long-range shots from the receiver, a chance created in law if not in spirit. As for the other game, well, it was against Manchester United. Ten-man Manchester United at that.

    Wirtz can still get locked out of high-leverage games against Arsenal and Manchester City. The Wirtz who, in Bayer Leverkusen colors, seemed the surest nine-figure bet in the game tended to excel whatever the opposition. For Liverpool, it has to be just right. A game that is more up and down with fewer demands on him to break down a low block. Opponents who are slightly less muscular than the Premier League average (see Manchester United). There is still a suspicion that a league as physical and fast as England's might lessen Wirtz's effectiveness, though the man himself would contend otherwise. He says he is getting used to the demands of the league.

    In a recent development, "I can't really say that I've changed that much," he noted when asked how he had adapted to life with Liverpool. "I've become a bit better on a physical level and that's the only reason that could explain it.".

    It has been revealed that credit also went to Andoni Iraola, who has afforded Wirtz a largely settled run as the primary creator in a 4-2-3-1. "He is bringing me back in a place where I was maybe two years ago where I played really good football," the German international mentioned. "I can feel that he gives me the confidence and I'm really happy about that. I'm just trying to give him back what he gives me.".

    Expect this good form to continue in Europe, where Wirtz has generally looked a more threatening player than he does in the Premier League. In part that's a function of the aforementioned physicality. It's probably also true that the likes of LASK, Villarreal, Qarabag and Wednesday's opponents Club Brugge would not exactly be pulling up trees in the Premier League either. A chance, then, for Wirtz to build even more momentum.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Working on one of the world's biggest football video games is the perfect combination of my two biggest passions, gaming and football.
    • I work on the creation of football video games.
    • We make sure everything works, and we work closely with the developers to try and make the most realistic simulation of football.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Working on one of the world's biggest football video games is the perfect combination of my two biggest passions, gaming and football.

    I'm CJ Ramson. I work on the creation of football video games. I work on Football Manager as an associate QA manager. QA stands for quality assurance.

    We're the ones that test the game. We make sure everything works, and we work closely with the developers to try and make the most realistic simulation of football.

    Growing up, I loved football, whether that was playing football or playing football video games with my friends. I'd always be doing one or the other. With the video games, the thing that really drew me to them was I've always been into the tactical side of the game, either being able to control the players or create your own tactics.

    Industry observers note that so a typical day for us, we'll get a fresh build in from the developers. We'll test it as a QA team, and we'll look for either bugsor ways that we can improve the game. That can be anything from the runs that players make, to decisions they make on the ball, what the team instructions and tactics do. So there's a lot of areas for us to cover. Our final goal is to make it as realistic to real football as possible.

    According to recent reports, so even though my background was in coaching, there was a lot of transferable skills that I learned and developed through my time coaching that I managed to transfer into this. So whether that's being really analytical and having a good eye for detail and knowingwhen to pick things out and what to look for, or it could be things like timekeeping and making sure things run perfectly on time, and working with other people as well. So social skills where you have to work within a team or even lead a team.

    The animation he makes, and the ball physics as well, where the ball goes off after the save.".

    Sources indicate that so as much as I loved playing football, I realised quite early on I probably wasn't going to be a professionalfootballer. But I wanted to work in football and find. So at college, I studied sports science, and that's where I found my love of coaching. I did my FA Level 1 and then went on to do my FA Level 2. After I left college, I got a job at Arsenal, which was unpaid, working with them, learning how to develop my coaching skills. Which then led to me having a full-time paid job at Fulham Football Club, working with the youth teams, working with the academy teams. And then that eventually led to me going to an event. I saw an opportunity where you could apply for a job in Football Manager. It was something that naturally I was interested in, had a conversation with them, and realised it was definitely something that I would love to do.

    Recent findings suggest that so I went to the networking event at Kick It Out, and that was an opportunity for me to network with other football coaches, other people within the gaming industries, and have a really good insight to different jobs in football gaming. Without doing that, I wouldn't have the opportunity to meet the people at Football Manager and see a new job in gaming, which I wouldn't have beenaware of.

    One of the highlights of my career so far is working on the in-and-out-of-possession system on FM 26. This is something we see in real football all the time, so being part of the team that brought that to life and brought it into the game was super cool.

    Working within the football industry is a dream come true. Being able to work on something that I'm passionate about, that is played and enjoyed by millions of people, is an amazing feeling for me and an amazing opportunity that I have. And yeah, I love it.

    To find out what other jobs you could have in football, explore the BBC Bitesize Follow Your Passion collection.

    It has been revealed that ever wondered who makes sure your video games are great? This guy!

    Recent findings suggest that CJ works as an associate quality assurance manager on the video game Football Manager. His team test the game to make sure everything works, and collaborate with the developers to create the most realistic simulation of football.

    There are lots of different ways to progress in the gaming industry.

    Recent findings suggest that CJ works in the QA (Quality Assurance) team, testing games. In this team, his career progression has followed this path:.

    QA tester --> QA lead --> QA manager.

    In a recent development, his team is just one of the options, though. "There are lots of other roles within the industry too, including production, game design, social media and development, where developers help to code the game," he explains. "Depending on your skills and interests, there are different pathways you can take that you might enjoy and be suited to.".

    There are different roles in video game testing. CJ notes that: "Salaries can vary depending on your role and the manufacturer you work for. They can range from around Â£20,000 to Â£50,000 and upwards." The higher salaries in this range could apply when you've gained more experienced and progressed in your career.

    CJ is now a quality assurance manager, but he started out as a quality assurance tester. Find out more about the role of QA tester below. This role can have various other job titles, such as games tester, computer games tester, and video games tester.

    Friedrich Christian "Mick" Flick, an art collector, investor and multimillionaire who belonged to one of Germany's richest business dynasties, has died aged 82 in Rosenheim in the southern state of Bavaria, his family has noted.

    The family said in a statement issued on Saturday that Flick left behind "the memory of a life shaped by significant acts of generosity as a donor and patron, particularly in contemporary art and in promoting tolerance.".

    Flick was the grandson of Friedrich Flick, who made a huge fortune in the Nazi era with his coal and steel business, partly by using forced labor.

    This past came back to haunt the grandson in 2003 when he pledged to loan his world-famous collection of modern art to Berlin, with the Central Council of Jews in Germany calling the Flick Collection a "Göring Collection" and saying the loan was intended to wash clean the "blood money" from the Nazi era.

    The collection, which contains some 2,500 works by 150 artists, was exhibited in parts in the German capital from 2004 to 2021.

    Flick later said in an interview that the widespread outrage, while hurtful, had forced him to look more closely at his family's history.

    According to his family, Flick once remarked: "I have no guilt for my forefathers' conduct, but I feel a responsibility, a very special responsibility. Every German bears this responsibility. As a Flick, I bear it twice.".

    Among other things, he collaborated with the Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation, which oversees Berlin's museums, to research his family's Nazi past.

    He also set up a foundation in Potsdam, near Berlin, that aimed to combat xenophobia and racism and contributed €5 million ($5.4 million) to the foundation to compensate former forced laborers.

    The family was also involved in a highly publicized party donations scandal in the 1980s that became known as the "Flick Affair.".

    Sources indicate that "Mick" Flick married Countess Maya von Schönburg (1958-2019), the older sister of well-known socialite, businesswoman, art collector and artist Gloria von Thurn und Taxis, in 1985. The couple had three children.

    German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier is setting off on a five-day trip to Africa that will take him to Ivory Coast, Ghana and Kenya.

    Steinmeier will be accompanied by a business delegation and is expected to focus on economic cooperation and the training of skilled workers during the trip.

    On Monday, Steinmeier is to be received by Ivorian President Allassane Outtara in Abidjan, Ivory Coast's largest city and seat of government.

    The next day, in the Ghanaian capital, Accra, he is set to open the German-African Business Summit, which, according to its website, "brings together senior business executives, policymakers, investors, and industry leaders from across Germany and Africa.".

    On Wednesday, he will be received by Kenyan President William Ruto in Nairobi.

    In Kenya, Steinmeier will also visit the Crescent Island Game Sanctuary on Thursday, the last day of his trip.

    The Federal Institute for Hydrology (BfG) has said it expects water levels in large rivers in western Germany, including the Rhine, to return to average or above in the next few days amid sustained rainfall.

    It said the water level at the key gauge in Kaub near Koblenz, located at an important bottleneck on the Middle Rhine, could reach some 3.3 meters (10.8 feet), more than 3 meters higher than the last recorded low-water readings.

    The BfG noted it also expected rising water levels in the Weser and Danube rivers, with smaller increases in the Elbe and Oder.

    The rising water level in the Rhine, an notable shipping route, means that conditions for water-borne cargo transport have improved, according to Germany's inland navigation association BDB.

    "The more abundant rainfall in the past days has caused the water level in the Rhine to rise considerably, and they will keep rising a great deal in the next few days as well, meaning that each ship has much more transport capacity again," noted Fabian Spiess, the deputy manager at BDB.

    In the middle of the year, many ships were forced to drastically reduce the loads they carried, leading to economic losses that will not be recuperated any time soon, according to Spiess.

    He cited the year 2018, in which shipping on the Rhine was also hindered by extremely low water levels, saying that the months of improved conditions at the end of that year had not been enough to make good the economic damage incurred.

    The conservation NGO also remarked that the current rain provided temporary relief to the environment but could not compensate for the negative consequences of the long dry period.

    It said species of animals, such as amphibians and water insects, that lived in small bodies of water and moist habitats had been particularly impacted.

    Justice Minister Stefanie Hubig indicates that she intends to tighten the law on murders committed with "gender-specific" motives, with a particular focus on femicides perpetrated by men who are unable to accept a separation or the desire of a woman to live a self-determined life.

    "A man kills, or attempts to kill, his partner or ex-partner almost every day in Germany," Hubig told the Sunday edition of the mass-circulation Bild newspaper.

    Sources indicate that "Any man killing a woman because she wants to leave him must be punished as a murderer," she said, noting that in some cases, courts cite a man's deep sadness or fear of losing a partner to someone else as extenuating circumstances. This can lead to a lesser conviction of manslaughter.

    She mentioned that in future, courts should look more closely at such motives to determine whether they were based on sentiments of patriarchal possessiveness.

    However, Hubig, who belongs to the center-left Social Democrats (SPD), said she was opposed to making femicide a separate category of crime, as some women's rights organizations have demanded.

    She stated that, in her opinion, doing so would have "no advantages over what we are intending — and much bigger disadvantages.".

    The proposals are currently being debated within the coalition government and are expected to be presented to the states and associations for consideration before the end of the year.

    They will then have to go before the Cabinet before being put before the parliament.

    Altogether, some 23,000 workers at 19 companies in northern Germany have been called upon to participate, including employees at automaker Mercedes-Benz, shipbuilding tech giant Meyer Werft and wind ​energy company Siemens Gamesa.

    The union remarked that a strike on Friday saw some 12,300 workers walk out at 17 facilities.

    It says that the strikes are meant to increase the pressure on employers to yield to its demands, which include a 5% ‌wage increase.

    So far, employers have ⁠offered a one-off payment next year and a 1.3% wage increase from July 2028.

    A latest goal celebration was devised by Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha after his previous one caused controversy due to its religious aspect.

    Recent findings suggest that after scoring the goal that secured Dortmund's 1-0 victory over Borussia Mönchengladbach (see entry below), Nmecha knelt on one knee and crossed his arms in front of his chest. He then spread his arms, appearing to pray with his eyes closed.

    Nmecha told broadcaster Sky that he intends to continue expressing his faith during goal celebrations, adding that he had once again given glory to Jesus.

    However, he did not perform the controversial part of his usual goal celebration. In it, he removes an imaginary crown from his head and places it on the pitch in front of him while kneeling.

    This celebration has been heavily criticized, even by Dortmund's fan department.

    Nmecha explained that the celebrations is about "putting down my 'crown' in front of the soon-to-come king and point out to Jesus, my hope and my strength.".

    The gesture is used by Ballers in God, a network of Christian football players that has been criticized for the homophobic and queerphobic statements made by its members.

    Dortmund president Hans-Joachim Watzke said he asked the player not to do the celebration again.

    Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha led his team to the top of the German Bundesliga table with a 1-0 victory over last-place Borussia Mönchengladbach.

    Bundesliga powerhouse Bayern Munich concluded the 2025-26 financial year with record figures.

    According to the financial report released Saturday at the club's annual general meeting, the club's total turnover was €988.2 million ($1.08 billion) — that is around €10 million more than the previous year.

    Operating profit (EBITDA) increased from €187.8 million to €190.8 million. Pre-tax profit was €35.3 million, and net profit for the year was €22.8 million.

    Bayern had a particularly strong year in terms of sponsorships. Turnover increased by nearly €30 million, reaching €268.4 million. The club also set a record in merchandise sales, earning €152.8 million.

    "We have achieved another record year," CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen said. "This indicates that our club has a strong foundation. And we continue to invest to ensure the best possible conditions for the sporting success of our teams.".

    Moreover, Bayern achieved another milestone. They reached 500,000 members — more than any other club in the world.

    Over the past 12 years, the German giants have doubled their membership, growing from 250,000 in 2014 to 500,000 this year.

    "Record champions, record members, record member champions," president Herbert Hainer mentioned.

    Members hold a 70% stake in the club, which is well above the simple majority required by German rules.

    The remaining 30% is owned by four German companies with roots in Bavaria: Adidas, Audi, Allianz, and Viessmann.

    Bayern won the league and cup double in the 2025-26 season, losing only three of 53 games across all competitions. In Europe, the club made it to the Champions League semifinals.

    By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

    Published: 12:15 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 14:05 EST, 26 November 2026.

    Swansea City have launched an internal investigation after an inappropriate image of one of its players was shared on social media.

    The image, which emerged on X, formerly Twitter, on Wednesday night, appeared to show a Swansea City player naked standing beside a bed.

    The photo, first taken on Snapchat, has since disappeared online after violating the social media site’s rules.

    A Swansea City spokesperson confirmed to Daily Mail Sport that the club are investigating the photo internally but no further comment will be made at this time.

    The photo, which was first shared by a Cardiff City fan, has emerged just days before this Sunday’s South Wales derby between Swansea and Cardiff, with tensions between both fanbases high now that they are back in the same division.

    Swansea City have released an internal investigation after an inappropriate image of one of its players was shared on social media.

    While Swansea blueprint to speak to the player to establish the key facts behind the image, there is also a legal side that cannot be ignored.

    In England and Wales it is a criminal offence to share naked or intimate photos without consent under Section 66B of the Sexual Offences Act 2003.

    Should an investigation determine the image has been tampered with, including AI-generated or manipulated 'deepfakes,' which was one of the allegations on social media on Wednesday night, that too is a criminal act under the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that have Paris Saint-Germain been defanged? It is too soon to say if injuries have laid low the Champions League's biggest beast, but on the evidence of Wednesday's 2-2 draw with Roma, there might not be quite the same fear factor when opponents find themselves face to face with the kings of Europe's jungle.

    Industry observers note that without Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue, both of whom are expected to miss most, if not all, of this season with knee injuries, there simply was not the final-third threat in PSG's ranks to keep Roma honest without the ball. That was all the more pronounced given that Ousmane Dembele was left on the bench until the penalty with which PSG took a 2-1 lead. Maghnes Akliouche, Senny Mayulu and Ferran Torres are talented forwards, the last good enough to win a World Cup final for Spain. Pair one or even two of them with the potential Ballon d'Or winners who started for PSG in the Champions League final, and the drop-off is not particularly significant.

    Of course, it might be that Luis Enrique is not particularly minded to see how good his reserves could be flanking Dembele. It would make sense. The Frenchman's fitness needs careful managing at the best of times. With PSG having won their first four league-phase games, there was no pressing need to load up minutes on a player who will surely be needed in the spring. It was a similar story at the base of PSG's team, Ilia Zabarnyi preferred to Marquinhos, another who does well to hit a dozen games before Christmas. This might be a vision of the months ahead for an injury-addled PSG, but it might just be a team that has never taken the league phase particularly seriously not taking the league phase particularly seriously.

    Industry observers note that whatever the longer-term view, on the field this evening, PSG's attack lacked the bite to keep Roma backing off. There is a good chance that any team managed by Gian Piero Gasperini might just go man-to-man whoever the opposition, but the fearlessness with which the Giallorossi hurtled around the Parc des Princes was a sure sign they weren't checking over their shoulder quite as much.

    Instead, they felt empowered to push on, center back Mario Hermoso on hand to roll in the opener inside the box after an excellent run by Matias Soule. Again, the caveat to assessing how future opponents might take on PSG is that Hermoso has been box-crashing from defense all through this season. You can't be sure he wouldn't have been in the same spot even if he were marking Doue or Kvaratskhelia.

    What you can know is that Roma's aggression when PSG had the ball in open play was not what cost them. Nuno Mendes' ability to blow by his man created challenges, and Achraf Hakimi got his usual shots and shot assists from advanced positions. They could have beaten Roma, but aside from the fullbacks and a few darts into the area by Joao Neves, there was not much to scare Mile Svilar in the champions' lineup.

    It has been revealed that instead, it was familiar failings that cost Roma, who might be a real dark horse for this competition when they can successfully defend a corner. Zabarnyi did not even have to win a duel to turn Mayulu's delivery home, just standing in the space between two white shirts at the near post. PSG's second, from the penalty spot, was a Roma confection too. Wesley could argue that Svilar should have been off his line quicker when Hakimi charged in behind, but did the Brazilian need to put his arms on his man at the exact moment he broke into the box? Wesley was lucky not to get a straight red.

    According to recent reports, in such favorable positions, prime PSG often blitz their opponents. This time, even with Dembele on the field, they could not get clear. Gasperini had an ace of his own on the bench, Donyell Malen sparking Roma after his introduction. A driving run and cutback from the left had PSG scrambling, Vitinha's arm blocking a shot to hand the visitors a penalty that Malen converted.

    Had a third goal come, it would probably have been for Roma, Hermoso blazing over late on. There was something more in this for Roma, who remain outside the top 24 despite such impressive displays against Real Madrid, Manchester United and now the holders. As for PSG, there will be time for Luis Enrique to work out how his side dominates Europe with its attack so limited. It would appear there is work to do.
