    Thomas Frank earns his first Crystal Palace victory as boss, Bournemouth win TENTH game in a row with comeback, and Brighton thrash Romanian minnows - but Sunderland are held at home

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2442 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

    ⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By LUKE POWER, SPORTS REPORTER and BEN WINSTANLEY and WILL PICKWORTH, SPORTS REPORTER and MILES STARFORTH.
    • Published: 15:09 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 19:33 EST, 26 November 2026.
    • Thomas Frank said he was happy to be 'back in the circus' at his Crystal Palace unveiling, yet when he found himself staring down the barrel at a second defeat in a week, he may have been rueing that statement.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By LUKE POWER, SPORTS REPORTER and BEN WINSTANLEY and WILL PICKWORTH, SPORTS REPORTER and MILES STARFORTH.

    Published: 15:09 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 19:33 EST, 26 November 2026.

    Thomas Frank said he was happy to be 'back in the circus' at his Crystal Palace unveiling, yet when he found himself staring down the barrel at a second defeat in a week, he may have been rueing that statement.

    But when Chris Richards' long-throw made its way to Jean-Philippe Mateta, everything changed on a chaotic night at Selhurst Park.

    The French forward was pulled down by Jon Martin, who was sent off, and after Mateta tucked away his penalty, a flat performance and atmosphere was transformed.

    Having been dominated, Palace were now quick, confident and incisive, and it was the Basque outfit who were on the ropes as Daichi Kamada saw an effort cleared off the line.

    Jorgen Strand Larsen then attempted an audacious bicycle kick which fell to the feet of Dwight McNeil yards out to send the home fans into delirium.

    It has been revealed that it could have been more, but Yeremy Pino's penalty in added time was saved and Strand Larsen missed an open goal. Dean Henderson then made a brilliant stop to secure the three points.

    Thomas Frank got his first win as Crystal Palace boss as his side came from behind to beat Real Sociedad 2-1.

    Palace's season has been a disaster thus far, but it now has lift-off, and most importantly belief, heading into Sunday's crunch clash with Hull.

    In a recent development, 'It could be (a turning point) but we need to follow it up with a good performance against Hull,' said Frank. 'But you can take a lot of positives. What I really liked is the belief from the players and that we were a threat on set pieces.

    In a recent development, 'The penalty and red card changed the game. It’s not easy 10 vs 11, but we were brave and it paid off - and then we were all close to a heart attack in the last five minutes!'.

    Frank, who received a warm reception from the Eagles faithful ahead of his first home game, handed rare starts to Will Hughes, Ben Chilwell and Eddie Nketiah as he rang the changes after last week’s defeat by Coventry.

    They practised defending set-pieces in the warm-up in an attempt to deal with what has become their kryptonite, yet Chelsea loanee Mamadou Sarr almost turned in at the far post from a free kick just minutes in.

    After a poor opening half hour, Sociedad stepped things up and Henderson was forced into a string of good saves. Palace’s midfield was struggling and the Basque outfit should have gone ahead when Mikel Oyarzabal somehow fired straight at Henderson from a few yards out.

    The England keeper had to be alert again soon after, yet the pressure paid off when Sarr turned home from Job Ochieng's cross.

    But the game changed with Mateta's intervention, before McNeil ensured that, despite the injury-time mayhem, Frank is more than happy to be back in the madhouse of management.

    According to recent reports, 'The feeling after a win on the pitch with players, staff and fans, but also in the changing room is so difficult to describe - it’s so unique,' said Frank. 'You like to experience a lot of that, but the hectic last 15 minutes, that was crazy.'.

    Recent findings suggest that 'The red card and penalty were the decisive action in the match,' added Sociedad boss Pellegrino Matarazzo. 'We controlled the match completely up until that. We tried to stabilise, but we could not hold them off long enough.'.

    In a recent development, can anybody stop Bournemouth? For long stretches here it looked as if their relentless march would finally be stopped - but the 10-man Cherries found another gear to continue their rampage.

    Marco Rose’s men have won 10 games in a row now, extending a club record. For two months, they have steamrolled their opponents with dauntless football and racked up an aggregate score of 25-3. They sit top of the Europa League with a perfect record.

    Underneath the red and black armour, fans are starting to wonder if these players are actually of our species. Is Justin Kluivert a man or a cyborg? If you prick James Hill, does he bleed?

    With each victory, the cry of the football world grows louder: somebody, please, stop this Bournemouth juggernaut, for the sake of everybody else’s trophy prospects.

    In a recent development, celta Vigo stepped up as the next challengers and thought they would be the heroes. They found Bournemouth’s net four times in all, but were denied by the offside flag for three of them. For long stretches, they were in command.

    Bournemouth have now won 10 games in a row after coming from behind to beat Celta Vigo 2-1.

    After a disappointing first half, Alvaro Rodriguez got them level early in the second.

    Rayan scored the winner against the run of play as Bournemouth continued their perfect run in the Europa League.

    In the first half, Bournemouth looked average. They were gifting away the ball in their own half, Celta found ways to sneak through their pincer-movement press, and the Spaniards had the better chances.

    The first red flag came 11 minutes in, when Michele Di Gregorio spilled a save into the path of Pablo Duran, who dinked over the goalkeeper but saw his effort ruled out for offside.

    Such warning bells were unheeded. Not long later, former Liverpool man Iago Aspas forced a save with a spectacular overhead kick at the age of 39.

    Bournemouth failed to clear their lines, and Aspas punished the visitors, ghosting past Alex Scott on his return from injury before blasting beyond Di Gregorio with his left foot.

    Things went from bad to worse minutes later when Bafode Diakite was sent off for a stamp on Couhaib Driouech, his yellow card upgraded to a red after a review by referee Harm Osmers.

    Celta almost doubled their lead when Duran beat Di Gregorio again, but he had strayed offside.

    In a recent development, the cameras panned to Rose, who stood looking bewildered on the sidelines, hands on hips. It took them 37 minutes for Kluivert to register their first shot. Bournemouth had been played off the park. This was a case of clinging on.

    But the side that emerged in the second half were unrecognisable. If Bournemouth were a man down, they played with all the swagger of having an extra body.

    They were level within two minutes of the restart, Alvaro Rodriguez glancing in from Amine Adli’s header.

    According to recent reports, suddenly Bournemouth were their efflorescent selves again. Antonio Silva, Adli, and Rodriguez combined for a beautiful passage of play but were spurned by the offside flag. Hill tested Ionut Radu from range.

    They finally got their rewards on the counter-attack, when Marcus Tavernier teed up his fellow substitute Rayan to slot past Radu and stun their hosts. Another comeback job complete.

    And so the Bournemouth army marches on unfettered. In the next nine days, they face Fulham, Brighton, and Hull in the Premier League. By the time they visit Arsenal in mid-December, they may be breathing down their necks.

    Earlier this week, Brighton CEO Paul Barber revealed the lengths that his club go to before agreeing to sign a player.

    'We try and talk to people that know them, people that have coached them, people that played with them, sponsors that have worked with them, media that have interviewed them, maybe even neighbours that have lived next door to them,' he told Men in Blazers media network. 'You know, what sort of people are we talking about? Are we talking about players that are entirely focused on their work?'.

    There can be little doubt that the rigorous selection process is working, and two of their budget buys were on the scoresheet in the first half as they made light work of the Romanian champions Universitatea Craiova - and continued to make a mockery of the supposed challenge of balancing domestic and European assaults.

    Industry observers note that in the third minute Ibrahim Osman - £16.6m from Nordsjaelland in 2024 – finished off a sharp team move from close range after a pinpoint Jack Hinshelwood cross. Then shortly after the half-hour mark full back Maxime de Cuyper, £17m from Club Brugge in 2025, seized on a slack defensive ball into midfield, took two touches in advancing forward and - still well outside the box – wrongfooted the goalkeeper as he stroked the ball into the far corner. He made the finish look much easier than it was.

    Brighton thrashed Romanian champions Universitatea Craiova and look capable of competing on multiple fronts.

    If the result was still in any doubt then, it wasn’t by the 39th minute when Vladimir Screciu was sent off for a clumsy challenge on Matt O’Riley. Referee Matthias Jollenbeck showed a yellow card but a replay showed a hefty tread on the ankle and - after being sent to his monitor - upgraded it to red.

    The second half, then, gave the Seagulls a chance to remind everyone of their ruthless side. Already the highest scorers in the Premier League - averaging 2.4 per game this season – they wasted little time adding to their tally.

    First, 19-year-old Charalampos Kostoulas made it three with his sixth of the season thanks to a cool finish on the hour mark, two minutes before Osman – like Hinshelwood a constant menace - picked the ball up on the left and cut inside to roll home his second.

    They ended 90 minutes of domination having had 27 shots – one of which saw Femi Azeez missing the chance to make it five on debut by inexplicably blazing over from five yards.

    Brighton have now scored four or more in five of their eight home games this season, and ended last night’s rout top of the Conference League having yet to concede a goal. The competition does not look big enough for them.

    Sunderland still have work to do if the club is to reach the Europa League’s knockout stages after Jagiellonia Bialystok held them to a 1-1 draw in a game which saw some supporters of the Polish club evade a UEFA ban and get into the Stadium of Light.

    Timur Tutierov’s second-half opener for Sunderland, hoping to secure a top-eight finish in the competition’s league phase and avoid the play-offs in their first European campaign in 53 years, was quickly cancelled out by the visitors.

    Recent findings suggest that ‘It’s clear we are making many unforced errors this season leading to goals,’ remarked head coach Regis Le Bris. ‘The last two games, it didn’t happen, which is good, and now this is a reminder you can’t relax.’.

    Jagiellonia supporters had been banned from the game following crowd disturbances at the club’s fixture away to Levski Sofia on November 5.

    But a number of visiting fans were removed from the stadium by police during the first half, and a “disappointed” Sunderland issued a statement after the game which claimed that Jagiellonia had “failed to engage and cooperate” with efforts to stop their supporters getting into home sections.

    Sources indicate that le Bris had gone into the game without injured captain Granit Xhaka and striker Brian Brobbey, two of his most influential players. Sunderland’s head coach, mindful of forthcoming Premier League games against Tottenham Hotspur, Liverpool and Newcastle United, took no chances with the pair for the visit of Jagiellonia, ninth in the Polish league.

    Sunderland had to settle for a 1-1 draw against Polish side Jagiellonia Bialystok.

    He made six changes from the team which had held Aston Villa to a goalless draw at the weekend, again fielding a youthful team in the competition.

    A flat performance from a much-changed team had seen Sunderland beaten 2-0 by Croatian champions Dinamo Zagreb in their last European outing at the Stadium of Light. The visiting section had been bouncing that night, in contrast to the empty seats for the visit of Jagiellonia.

    On Wearside, the feeling ahead of the match was that third-bottom Sunderland, while shot shy, were slowly turning a corner, having taken four points from fixtures against Chelsea and Villa without conceding a goal to climb above Manchester United in the table.

    The massive one in Europe - AC Milan at the San Siro - is next in the competition for Sunderland, with the fixture having captured the imagination of supporters.

    There were scarves with the slogan ‘Have you ever seen a Mackem in Milan? You’re about to!’ on sale outside the ground, with the merchandise a nod to a song which fans of their rivals Newcastle United can no longer sing.

    Sunderland had an early scare when a Nik Prelec shot took a deflection off Ndah Sidiki, but Robin Roefs was able to gather the ball.

    Within minutes of the game starting, it became apparent that a group of Polish fans had managed to buy tickets in the North Stand, and police were promptly called to remove them from the stadium amid cheers from Sunderland supporters.

    On the pitch, it was another slow start for Le Bris’ side, though Malick Fofana tested Slawomir Abramowicz with a fine left-footed shot from outside the box.

    Timur Tutierov was on target fo the Black Cats, but this was a flat performance.

    Industry observers note that enzo Le Fee did well to seize on a back pass in the 30th minute and cross from the left for Nilson Angulo - who was unmarked in the box - after rounding the goalkeeper. However, his shot struck the feet of Yuki Kobayashi.

    Omar Alderete was forced off as the half-time break approached, and Roefs beat away a free-kick from Kajetan Szmyt.

    Sunderland went into the break knowing they should have led, but their finishing had again let them down in the absence of Brobbey, their talisman.

    In a recent development, le Bris’ team were ahead within seconds of the restart. Rigg broke through the middle, and the ball was worked to Le Fee, whose cross bounced off a visiting defender on its way to Tutierov at the far post, who headed home.

    The lead did not last, with Kamil Jozwiak seizing on a Nilson Reinildo backpass before rounding Roefs to level.

    Roefs denied Jozwiak at the hour-mark with a low save as home fans became increasingly frustrated with their team.

    A frustrated Le Bris stated: ‘It’s hard to take, because we would like to have better football, better expression.’.

    England are a seeded side for the Nations League quarter-finals after topping their group.

    The draw for the final eight teams in the 2026-27 Nations League will be on Friday, 20 November at 11:00 GMT.

    It will take place at Uefa's headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland and be broadcast on Uefa TV.

    England are the only home nation to have made it to the quarter-final stage, however Northern Ireland's draw against Hungary saw them top Group B2 and secure promotion to League A in the 2028-29 tournament.

    Scotland will remain in League B following their third-place finish in Group B1, and Wales face a League A/B relegation play-off in March after being consigned to last place in Group A4.

    The Republic of Ireland finished second in Group B3 and so will take part in a League A/B promotion play-off in March.

    The winners of groups A1-A4 are seeded for the draw, playing the runners-up of other groups in League A.

    England have sealed their place in the last eight as Group A3 winners and could face:.

    They cannot face A3 runners-up Spain as teams must be drawn against sides from other groups.

    The quarter-finals will be played over two legs during the international break between 25-30 March.

    Seeded teams get to play the second leg of their quarter-final at home.

    Nations that reach the semi-finals can bid those penultimate matches as well as the final.

    The remaining dates for the Nations League are:.

    Quarter-finals first leg: 25-27 March.

    Quarter-finals second leg: 28-30 March.

    Semi-finals, third-place play-off and final: 9-13 June.

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    Why Man City can't wear their fresh kit in Premier League

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (388 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Manchester City will only be wearing their orange kit for selected Champions League games.
    • Manchester City sported a newly introduced orange fourth kit during their Champions League draw with Napoli on Tuesday - but will not be able to wear it in the Premier League.
    • Top-flight clubs in England can only wear a maximum of three strips in a league campaign, meaning Enzo Maresca's side cannot play in their new kit.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Manchester City will only be wearing their orange kit for selected Champions League games.

    Manchester City sported a newly introduced orange fourth kit during their Champions League draw with Napoli on Tuesday - but will not be able to wear it in the Premier League.

    Top-flight clubs in England can only wear a maximum of three strips in a league campaign, meaning Enzo Maresca's side cannot play in their new kit.

    However, there is no limit in the Champions League, meaning City can wear their fresh strip for the rest of their European campaign.

    City can also wear the kit in the FA Cup, provided that an application is made to the Football Association, as well as a reason for its requested use.

    That is why Arsenal were allowed to play in a white fourth strip in the 2025-26 FA Cup as part of their campaign to combat youth knife crime in London.

    Fans could scan the badge on City's 2025-26 fourth kit to receive items in a video game.

    City also released a green fourth kit in 2025-26 with a gaming-inspired theme.

    The kit, debuted during their Champions League victory over Villarreal, featured an NFC chip in the club badge that fans could scan to unlock gaming rewards.

    The club released another fourth kit in the 2024-25 season co-designed by Noel Gallagher in tribute to the 30th anniversary of Oasis' 1994 album 'Definitely Maybe'.

    It was worn in the Champions League by the men's team against Inter Milan and Paris St-Germain, and the women's team against Paris FC and Barcelona.

    A fifth kit was also used by the men's team during the 2025 Club World Cup.

    During the 2023-24 season, the women's side also sported a Chinese Newly introduced Year-inspired shirt in a League Cup victory against rivals Manchester United.

    While the Premier League is more restrictive over the number of kits that can be released - the rules are more relaxed in other European leagues.

    Napoli wore 13 strips during the 2021-22 season; including a Halloween kit, four different Diego Maradona tributes and four Europa League-specific kits.

    Latest Update: An in situ redox-converted molecule for all-perovskite tandem solar cells

    📅 28 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (590 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that all-perovskite tandem solar cells (TSCs) are gaining prominence due to their ability to surpass the efficiency limit of single-junction perovskite solar cells (PSCs)1,2.
    • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
    • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that all-perovskite tandem solar cells (TSCs) are gaining prominence due to their ability to surpass the efficiency limit of single-junction perovskite solar cells (PSCs)1,2. However, the efficiency and stability of all-perovskite TSCs are limited by chemical instability at the hole transport layer/perovskite interface in the tin-lead (Sn-Pb) narrow-bandgap subcell, which introduces deep trap states from tin cations and promotes non-radiative recombination3-5. Here we incorporate a redox-converted molecule of p-aminobenzohydrazide (ABH) into poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS) that neutralizes PSS acidity, heals Sn4+ defects, and generates a dipole passivation effect upon oxidation. During the preparation of Sn-Pb perovskites, ABH suppresses interfacial oxidation by reducing Sn4+ defects and converts to p-aminobenzaldehyde (ABD), which suppresses photogenerated hole-induced Sn2+ oxidation, aligning energy levels for efficient hole extraction. The in situ redox-converted molecule stabilizes the buried interface during both device fabrication and operation, reduces non-radiative recombination and enhances stability. The resulting narrow-bandgap Sn-Pb PSC achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.4% (certified 25.2%) with an open-circuit voltage of 0.92 V and a fill factor of 83.4%. Integrated into monolithic all-perovskite TSCs, the device delivers a PCE of 31.1% (certified 30.8%) together with enhanced thermal (ISOS-D-2I, 85 °C) and operational stability (ISOS-L-1I) under inert conditions.

    Any regrets, Mauricio? Man Utd are deep in relegation battle after Anfield farce

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 28 min read (5692 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~28 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Liverpool fans did not miss a beat.
    • The Pochettino bandwagon rolled into town with the usual fanfare of a new era, new belief, new hope; and then the wheels came off, the doors collapsed and the engine exploded.
    • In that time, away to Liverpool of all places, they were 2-0 down, a player down – and down and out.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Liverpool fans did not miss a beat. They never do. “Poch is at the wheel,” they goaded as this calamity unfolded. But at the wheel of what, a clown car? The look of thunder on Mauricio Pochettino’s face remarked it all as he got off to the worst start of any Manchester United manager – or head coach – in 100 years.

    The Pochettino bandwagon rolled into town with the usual fanfare of a new era, new belief, new hope; and then the wheels came off, the doors collapsed and the engine exploded. The opening quarter of an hour really was that farcical.

    In that time, away to Liverpool of all places, they were 2-0 down, a player down – and down and out. If Pochettino had any uncertainty over the scale of the task ahead of him, there it was laid bare. Of course United had some mitigation. They played almost the entire game with 10 men, but teams have coped with that before and shown far more resistance and resilience. By the time United did that, it was game over. No one expected a quick fix, but come on.

    Any regrets, Mauricio? Whatever the salary, he could be forgiven for having a few as he watched on. This is a far cry from being in charge of the United States and watching them roll over Haiti 8-0 on aggregate, as he did last week. If Liverpool had been more ruthless, it could have been 8-0 here.

    Recent findings suggest that in the end it was 4-0 – the same scoreline by which Lal Hilditch lost his first game at United, away to Bolton Wanderers in October 1926. Hilditch was a stop-gap player-manager and former central defender Pochettino may well have been tempted to bring himself on, even at the age of 54. He could barely have done worse.

    Pochettino, too, can take some responsibility. Eyebrows were certainly raised when he dropped Harry Maguire – who he then had to bring on after 22 minutes – to hand Matthijs de Ligt his first Premier League start in 357 days. De Ligt was then at fault for the first and, arguably, the second goal.

    It has been revealed that did the head coach start with a back three or a back four? The players seemed confused. It eventually ended up as a back five.

    According to recent reports, but this was a collective failing for United. From the top – with director of football Jason Wilcox caught on camera with his head buried in his coat – through the club and out on the pitch. Pochettino is major on building a culture. So he has to abolish the comedy and the chaos and restore credibility.

    Recent findings suggest that united are deep in a relegation battle. Have no doubt. Eight points after 11 games means they are at the moment on target for fewer than 28 points, which is a lower points-per-game total than when they were relegated in 1974.

    In a recent development, the work needed at United is monumental. The transfer strategy has been inexplicable, with the decision being to rebuild the attack last year, the midfield this summer and wait until next year to remodel the defence. The folly of that has been exposed by the fact that United have conceded 34 goals already this season, the most in the top five European leagues.

    In a recent development, united will argue, with justification, that Leny Yoro’s eighth-minute sending-off for denial of a goalscoring opportunity was harsh given that Alexander Isak appeared to have already lost control of the ball. But what was Yoro thinking as he bundled into the back of the forward? And what was De Ligt doing as he watched on, or lumbered on, after failing to track the run from Ronald Araújo’s ball over the top?

    Industry observers note that leny Yoro is SENT OFF after eight minutes! 😱 https://t.co/VKYvckvBBP.

    In a recent development, and what were United doing with that shambolic defensive wall, with Bruno Fernandes left waving a leg as Dominik Szoboszlai could not believe his luck at the space he saw? The Liverpool midfielder simply whipped a low free-kick into the corner of the net.

    Dominik Szoboszlai SLAMS home the free-kick! 💥 https://t.co/Q09eEi0m0B.

    The second goal highlighted that mismatch as Rio Ngumoha easily beat Diogo Dalot, not for the first or last time, and pulled back a cross that Florian Wirtz hooked in off the crossbar. De Ligt was all over the place as he again watched on.

    It can be argued that, after that calamitous start, Pochettino stemmed the bleeding just as it appeared set to be a bloodbath. But that may also have owed much to a lack of killer instinct from Liverpool, who did not go for the jugular.

    "This is how they dreamt it here!" ❤️ Florian Wirtz doubles Liverpool's lead. https://t.co/RQbA6OXRLA.

    Into the second half and the chant from the Kop was clear. “Attack, attack, attack,” rang out as they demanded more goals; more humiliation and a repeat of the 7-0 from three years ago.     Bruno Fernandes says he has shelved talks over a new contract because it is not the “right moment” for discussions over his future as Manchester United captain.

    Fernandes, 32, is out of contract next summer although United have a 12-month option to extend his deal to 2028.

    The Portugal midfielder is understood to have rejected two contract offers from United since the summer but said all his focus needs to be on trying to help the team out of their current plight.

    United head into Sunday’s game against Liverpool at Anfield second from bottom in the Premier League.

    “We spoke about the contract at the end of last season,” Fernandes told Sky Sports.

    “We came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don’t think it’s the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations.

    “The most crucial thing now is that the club gets back to winning games.”.

    In a recent development, fernandes remarked claims he wants more money or a longer-term deal on offer are incorrect and that if finances were the matter he would have left Old Trafford before now. The captain has previously rejected lucrative offers from Saudi Arabia.

    “The club offered me a newly introduced contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay,” he said.

    Recent findings suggest that “There’s no negotiations ongoing, but I’ve seen people saying that ‘He’s asked for more money, he’s asked for more years’. If I wanted more money, I wouldn’t be here.

    “I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester.

    “Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here.

    “The thing is, I’ve always highlighted how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club. And I always said, in the moment the club thinks it’s time for me to move on, I will move on.

    It has been revealed that “I’m not going to be the player that I’ve seen many in this time at Manchester United. They’re going to stay here just by staying, just finish my contract and then we will see. In the moment the club notes, ‘Bruno, it’s time to part ways’, I’m going to be the first one walking out the door.”.

    United chief executive Omar Berrada said of Fernandes on Friday that it was “true that we’re having conversations about his fresh contract” but that the club preferred “to keep that private”.

    Having been voted PFA Player of the Year last season, Fernandes’ form has dropped off this term like that of the team.

    He was dropped for the 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth in the wake of a 4-1 drubbing by Como when he criticised the tactics and approach of then head coach Michael Carrick.

    Mauricio Pochettino, Carrick’s successor, confirmed on Friday that Fernandes would remain as captain.

    Fernandes noted the United fans had been “far too patient with us” and hopes Pochettino - who wanted to bring the Portuguese to Spurs in 2019 - will bring a fresh energy.

    “He’s someone that likes to bring a very good energy to the team, someone very positive, very strong, strict, noted it straight away that he won’t allow us to not give him what he demands from the team, from each player,” Fernandes said.

    “He wants the club to succeed so much, he wants to win games, and that’s pretty clear and obvious by the way he and his staff speak and want us to improve.

    According to recent reports, “Obviously [in 2019] I was a very young player that was eager to come to the Premier League. They had [Harry] Kane there, they had Dele Alli, Son, the chance of playing with those players in front was very attractive.”.

    Mauricio Pochettino has outlined his vision of changing the culture at Manchester United in his attempt to lift the club out of the Premier League relegation zone.

    Sources indicate that pochettino arrived in the country on Wednesday after his final matches in charge of the US national team. He has inherited a squad with some players who have publicly criticised their own coach and technical director this season during their slide down the table.

    The new United head coach, who has a contract until 2029, mentioned “culture” seven times in his first club interview in a pointed analysis of the work he needs to do at Old Trafford, starting with this weekend’s match against Liverpool at Anfield.

    “The culture, to create the culture is the most important,” Pochettino noted. “To have the culture is the most important. Create the habit, the principle and I think that is what we want to create. We need to look forward and to find a way to create the best habit and the culture that makes us to be close to win every single game.”.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    This blog is now closed. Read below for more on these stories and all other things Germany on Monday, November 23.

    Thank you for following our coverage of headlines from Germany on Monday, November 24.

    Industry observers note that the Federal President’s latest major trip takes him to Africa. Frank-Walter Steinmeier has just visited the Ivory Coast and is continuing on to Ghana and Kenya. His goal: to encourage more German companies to invest in Africa.

    Frank-Walter Steinmeier has visited 31 African countries during his political career. Even as foreign minister, he traveled regularly to the continent; as federal president, he has made twelve trips so far.

    From early on, he viewed Africa not only through the lens of development aid and humanitarian support, but also — much like former Chancellor Angela Merkel — as a market for the German economy that has been underutilized thus far. In 2015, as foreign minister in the Merkel administration, Steinmeier played a central role in the creation of the German-African Economic Summit.

    On his current trip as well, Steinmeier is advocating for greater German engagement in Africa. In Abidjan, the capital of the Ivory Coast, following a meeting with Ivorian President Alassane Ouattara, he called on German companies to step outside their comfort zone and take greater advantage of the opportunities offered by the country and the continent.

    The Ivory Coast is considered a location with growing potential. Despite its proximity to the Sahel region, which is plagued by terrorism, the country is relatively stable politically. The economy is growing by about six percent annually. Germany has more intensive trade relations with the Ivory Coast than with any other country in sub-Saharan Africa, and nowhere else in sub-Saharan Africa do so many people learn German — an advantage for German small and medium-sized enterprises — all of which both presidents emphasized very clearly during their meeting in Abidjan.

    In a recent development, up next, Steinmeier is scheduled to visit Accra, Ghana, for the sixth German-African Economic Summit, where more than 600 business representatives are expected to attend. As the summit’s initiator, the Federal President will open the event together with the host, Ghanaian President John Mahama. He will be accompanied by a ten-member business delegation representing industry, the financial sector, and energy consulting.

    The Economic Summit is taking place at a time when Germany’s relations with African countries are undergoing fundamental changes. In light of geopolitical shifts, Africa is increasingly coming into focus as an economic and trade partner.

    It has been revealed that the continent’s share of German foreign trade at the moment stands at just under 2%, or around €30 billion. At the same time, German exports to Africa are rising by at least 6% annually. And since Germany’s economy aims to reduce its dependence on China in the future, opportunities in Africa are growing.

    From Ghana, Frank-Walter Steinmeier will travel on to Kenya, the final stop on his tour of Africa.

    Environment Minister Carsten Schneider on Monday vowed that Germany will continue to move away from burning fossil fuels despite the failure of the COP31 declaration in Antalya, Turkey, this weekend.

    Speaking at an event in Potsdam, Schneider stated: "We will clearly maintain our course on climate protection in Europe and Germany, but above all one that makes us independent of oil and gas because otherwise we are vulnerable to blackmail and our economic performance becomes extremely volatile.".

    Schneider expressed disappointment less at the result of the two-week conference than its format, which he stated was far more focussed on spectacle than substance.

    It has been revealed that speaking of his vision for a format for future climate conferences, Schneider remarked: "Basically, I don't need so many people there. What I need are the relevant decision makers with whom I negotiate and make decisions.".

    Although he voiced relief that the final document from the conference had not represented a step backwards — as well as stressing that some 30 countries had pledged to maintain the move away from fossil fuels — Schneider acknowledged that it had been nearly impossible to find consensus with Russia and Saudi Arabia at the table.

    To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

    German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius urged calm over reports that Russia was planning to launch a nuclear-armed satellite into space as early as next month.

    "First of ​all, ‌let's remain calm, because there are reports — that's true — but ‌it's ​not clear what kind of weapons these are, and the ​effect they might have depends, in ⁠turn, ​on where they ​are deployed," Pistorius told ​reporters in ‌Berlin.

    In a recent development, "Therefore, it's too early to ​speculate ⁠publicly about this. We are consulting ⁠internally ​and taking the necessary measures.".

    German public broadcasters NDR and WDR and newspaper Süddeutsche Zeitung first reported on the matter, which noted that internal intelligence reports circulated among NATO countries earlier this month said that Russia was ready to bring the alleged satellite, named Sputnik-S, out of storage in Moscow.

    The reports noted Russia may be planning to launch it as soon as December.

    Nuclear weapons are banned in orbit by the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, of which Moscow is a signatory.

    German Chancellor Friedrich Merz remarked not allowing Ukraine intoNATO in 2008 was a mistake.

    At the2008 summit in Bucharest, Romania, German Chancellor Angela Merkel and French President Nicolas Sarkozy argued that they weren't ready to extend NATO membership to Ukraine.

    According to recent reports, US President George W. Bush said he was in favor of having Ukraine enter into NATO.

    But both Germany and France mentioned that that would hurt relations with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

    The NATO summit then decided that Ukraine would eventually join the alliance, but offered no timetable.

    At a press conference on Monday, Merz was asked about whether he thinks the time was right to talk about Ukraine's membership in NATO.

    To which Merz stated, "If it [Ukraine] had become a member of NATO, this war could probably have been prevented.".

    Merz meant Russia's war against Ukraine when he stated "this war" at the press conference after a meeting with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte.

    Angela Merkel defended her decision at the Bucharest summit as of 2024 as well, saying a large proportion of the Ukrainian population had opposed joining NATO at the time.

    German Chancellor Friedrich Merz called on Russia to end its "dangerous provocations" after two Russian missiles and a jet-powered drone crashed in Poland on Friday.

    Merz delivered those remarks after having met with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte in Berlin on Monday.

    Industry observers note that "Poland can count on our full solidarity. And if necessary, NATO will of course defend every inch of allied territory," Merz said.

    Merz said Europe and NATO must strengthen their defenses.

    Drones have repeatedly strayed into NATO airspace in the year since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

    The incident also came at a time as Poland was hosting a two-week military exercise by Ukraine's allies.

    German startup investments in fields such as robotics and defense are set to almost triple this year, a study noted on Monday.

    The German Start-up Association and the Joachim Herz Foundation study predicted that investments in so-called "deep tech startups" will surge from just €2.9 billion ($3.17 billion) last year to 8.1 billion ($8.9 billion) this year.

    The study described the rise as a "major success for Germany as a business location.".

    "Deep tech" typically refers to developing cutting-edge technologies based on scientific research, such as AI, biotechnology and quantum computing.

    A handful of massive fundraising rounds by firms including humanoid robot developer Neura Robotics,  AI drone maker Helsing and defense tech group Quantum Systems drove the investment boom.

    The study also showed about 300 upcoming deep tech startups are expected to be founded this year, a 40% rise compared with last year.

    Newly found startups tend to be founded around economic hubs like Berlin and Hamburg, which are also home to leading universities and research institutes.

    The study also highlighted challenges, including limited funding compared with their US counterparts and insufficient support to move startups from the laboratory to the real world.

    Police in several locations across Germany reported large numbers of bomb threats targeting schools.

    They noted that while they were investigating the claims, they did not initially have reason to treat them as credible threats.

    More than 400 schools in the southwestern state of Baden-Württemberg received threats, and more than 250 in Saxony-Anhalt received the emails, with several other regions also targeted on Monday morning.

    Similar reports have also emerged to the north of Germany, in Denmark.

    As in Germany, Danish police stated they did not believe the threats were credible, "but they understandably create insecurity locally at the schools.".

    Read more about the disruptive incidents that have targeted Europe in recent weeks.

    Germany's Freie Wähler (Free Voters) party have chosen a new chairman, weeks after their former front man Hubert Aiwanger unexpectedly passed away on November 4.

    Industry observers note that the party announced on Monday that Bavaria's Digital Affairs Fabian Mehring is to succeed Aiwanger both as party leader on the federal level and as one of two co-chairs of the Bavaria section of they party. The second state co-chair still needs to be decided.

    Aiwanger was found dead in a Berlin hotel room at the age of 55 with no foul play suspected. He's been the party's defining figure for almost four decades, having led the Free Voters to substantial success, especially in Bavaria.

    In a recent development, the Free Voters are originally a grass roots party in Bavaria and sit on the conservative edge of the political spectrum. They've been in government in Bavaria as junior coaltion partners of the Christian Social Union (CSU), sister party to Chancellor Merz's Christian Democratic Union (CDU).

    Recent findings suggest that there are also changes in the Bavarian state government. Tobias Gotthardt is to take over as economy minister, while Environment Minister Thorsten Glauber is set to become deputy premier behind Bavaria state Premier Markus Söder. The appointments still require formal approval by party conventions.

    German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul has inisted that NATO was ready to defend itself in the face of potential Russian threats against any of its member states.

    "We will always defend every inch of our NATO territory," Wadephul mentioned at the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin.

    His comments come after three Russian projectiles violated Polish airspace on Friday and crashed in the southeast of the country.

    Wadephul is attending the NATO assembly in Berlin and DW has   a dedicated blog on those talks  where you can read all about how Russia's war in Ukraine is taking center stage for the defense alliance.

    A massive strike is underway in Germany hitting major car brands another manufacturing factors. Metal and electrical workers are demanding better pay ahead of upcoming wage talks later this week. The strike has been initiated by IG Metall, Germany’s biggest and most powerful union.

    Famous car brands Mercedes and BMW  were affected as was an Opel plant, which is part of the international Stellantis group.

    The strikes began on Friday and are due to continue until Tuesday. Wage negotiations are then set to continue on Wednesday with another round of collective bargaining for some 3.7 million workers across the sector.

    The union is demanding a pay rise of 5% over one year while the employers association, Gesamtmetall, has offered a one-time payment and a pay increase of 1.3%.

    The tough struggle over wages comes as especially the German car industry is facing serious headwinds because of higher energy prices, US tariffs and mounting Chinese competition.

    A German investigative media report published on Monday claims that Russia would be able to launch a nuclear-armed satellite, called Sputnik-S, into orbit within the space of about 60 days if it wished.

    The report from public broadcasters WDR, NDR and the Süddeutsche Zeitung newspaper, cites a warning from German and other western intelligence agencies that it states was circulated at the start of November.

    It stated that a launch "could" take place by December, without quoting the document or clarifying whether it was talking only about a Russian capability, or a more firm intention.

    The report said the satellite itself had been built several years ago and was being stored in the Moscow area.

    German authorities did not respond to requests for comment on the record while the Russian Embassy in Berlin said the claims were part of a "propaganda" campaign.

    The report matches longstanding warnings, mainly but not exclusively from the US, that Russia could be preparing a nuclear strike in Earth orbit designed to take out a large number of satellites.

    This could have a severe impact on intelligence, communications, logisticts, navigation and other key services.

    Russia's war in Ukraine, and the Ukrainian military's reliance on the Starlink satellite internet service, has provided an additional reminder of the strategic significance of satellites in orbit.

    German exports to Africa have reached a new record. That’s according to a fresh study just as the country's president embarks on a trip to several African countries.

    Exports are expected to rise by 6% in 2026 to reach about 30 billion euros ($33bn).

    What’s behind the growing demand are especially orders from South Africa, Egypt, Tunisia, Nigeria, Angola and Kenya — countries where inflation has been dropping and exchange rates are more stable.

    According to recent reports, the biggest single export at the moment is a high-speed train network to Egypt. Other main exports include electrical equipment, optical instruments, plastics and pharmaceuticals, as well as food products, including dairy goods, cereals and baked goods.

    The data is being reported by the Reuters news agency, based on the government-owned agency Germany Trade & Invest (GTAI), which promotes foreign trade and investment in Germany.

    In 2025, exports to Africa had risen by 8% while in 2024 it had gone down.

    The Germangovernment has blamed oil and gas-producing nations for the COP climate conference ending without an agreement.

    "The oil and gas industry is still dragging its feet," German Environment Minister Carsten Schneider remarked after the UN climate talks had failed on Sunday. "Some oil-producing nations realize that the situation is becoming serious for them — that is why they are blocking it so vehemently," saidSchneider.

    Almost two days into overtime, the COP31 climate talks in Turkey ended on Sunday as many countries, including the EU, rejected a final declaration.

    Industry observers note that major sticking points at the summit included a commitment to accelerate global electrification and whether or not to explicitly mention looks to phase out fossil fuels. The suggested final declaration put forward by the COP presidency did not mention fossil fuels and according to critics would have undermined the shift away from fossil fuels.

    "I understand that this poses a threat to the business model of those countries that sell us oil and gas. But electrification will make the world a more peaceful and stable place," Schneider said.

    The inability to agree on a final declaration comes as climate change is increasingly linked to worsening heatwaves, floods and other natural catastrophes.

    German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier begins a five-day trip to Africa that will take him to Ivory Coast, Ghana and Kenya with a focus on economic cooperation and the training of skilled workers.

    He begins in Abidjan, where he is due to meet Ivorian President Alassane Ouattara. Steinmeier will also visit a vocational college and the International Academy for Counter-Terrorism before travelling on to Ghana.

    In the capital Accra on Tuesday, he is set to open the German-African Business Summit, which according to its website, "brings together senior business executives, policymakers, investors, and industry leaders from across Germany and Africa.".

    His final stop will be Kenya, where he will meet President William Ruto in Nairobi on Wednesday.

    The German president is traveling with a German business delegation and wants to encourage closer economic ties and greater investment in Africa.

    The trip is his 11th to sub-Saharan Africa and his final one as president as his term in office due to end next March.

    Why are there 2:05pm kick-offs in the Premier League on Sunday?

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (255 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Everton's derby with Liverpool has been moved from Saturday to Sunday.
    • The Premier League kick-off times look a little unusual this weekend, with no Saturday 12:30 GMT slot, and games starting at 12:00 and 14:05 on Sunday.
    • In a recent development, everton will host local rivals Liverpool on Sunday at 12 noon because the match has been selected for live broadcast by TNT, who have a mid-day broadcast slot on that day.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Everton's derby with Liverpool has been moved from Saturday to Sunday.

    The Premier League kick-off times look a little unusual this weekend, with no Saturday 12:30 GMT slot, and games starting at 12:00 and 14:05 on Sunday.

    In a recent development, everton will host local rivals Liverpool on Sunday at 12 noon because the match has been selected for live broadcast by TNT, who have a mid-day broadcast slot on that day. The game was originally scheduled for Saturday.

    This has had a knock-on effect on the remaining fixtures.

    On a typical Premier League weekend, the first matches will begin at 14:00 followed by a final 16:30 kick-off.

    Pushing start times back five minutes to 14:05 reduces the risk of overlap with the unusual early 12:00 start time, while avoiding clashing with the 16:30 fixture.

    Midweek European games have also affected the schedule, as the Premier League aims to prevent clubs from playing two matches within 60 hours of each other.

    Crystal Palace, Sunderland, Bournemouth and Brighton are all set to play in the Europa and Conference Leagues on Thursday, ruling them out of Saturday Premier League fixtures.

    Full Premier League schedule for Sunday, 29 November.

    Crystal Palace v Hull City (14:05).

    By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

    Published: 05:37 EST, 27 November 2026 | Updated: 07:24 EST, 27 November 2026.

    Manuel Neuer's estranged wife Anika has shared a post declaring that 'cheating on pregnant women is a whole different level of evil' following her split from the Bayern Munich and Germany star.

    The couple, who had a civil wedding in 2023 and held a larger wedding celebration in 2025, welcomed the birth of their second son in late August.

    German newspaper Bild reported that Neuer had informed Anika that he no longer wished to continue their marriage days after the birth.

    Neuer has since been photographed with an unidentified woman, who BILD reported as being a 23-year-old physiotherapist that the goalkeeper has worked with.

    The goalkeeper was spotted with the woman in Brazil this month, but reports have since emerged that they had also been seen on holiday in Sicily back in September.

    While Anika did not specifically accuse Neuer and there is no evidence to suggest he has been unfaithful, she has since reposted a message on social media which criticised men who have cheated on their pregnant partners.

    Manuel Neuer reportedly informed his wife Anika he wanted to end their marriage days after the birth of the couple's second child.

    Anika reshared a post on social media which criticised men who cheat on their pregnant partners.

    It has been revealed that the couple had their second child in August. Pictured: Anika watching Bayern Munich training in July.

    'Cheating on a pregnant woman is a whole different level of evil,' the post read.

    'Imagine looking at the woman carrying your child, watching her body change, seeing her struggle, get tired, and go through everything that comes with pregnancy and you still have the audacity to betray her behind her back.

    'She's carrying YOUR child while you're out there entertaining someone else. The woman who should be feeling loved, protected, and supported is instead left dealing with pain that you caused.

    According to recent reports, 'That's not a 'mistake.' That's a choice. A selfish, heartless, disrespectful choice.

    'If you can betray the woman carrying your own child, especially when she needs you the most, you don't just lack loyalty, you lack basic decency and respect.

    Neuer, who reportedly moved out of the family home in October, has not spoken publicly about the separation or reports of a new relationship.

    The 40-year-old, who is right now recovering from injury, has faced a backlash in Germany with relationship counsellor Ruth Marquardt accusing him of 'abandoning his wife and children'.

    The Germany and Bayern Munich goalkeeper married Anika in 2023 with the couple having two children.

    Anika, who is Neuer's second wife, is a professional handball player but halted her career in 2025 to focus on parenting.

    Neuer has faced a backlash in Germany following reports of his split from Anika.

    The post was liked by the wives of Neuer's Bayern Munich team-mates Joshua Kimmich and Konrad Laimer, as well as the goalkeeper's ex-wife Nina, who he separated from in 2020.

    Neuer has also been criticised by Germany and Bayern Munich legend Lothar Matthaus on his show 'Lothar Takes Off'.

    'It's certainly not something they discuss in the locker room, but I understand - we do have freedom of speech in Germany - that a wife of Joshua Kimmich or Konrad Laimer might like the video, because I think they can perhaps empathise with the situation, that it's not good for Mrs. Neuer in any way,' Matthaus noted.

    Industry observers note that 'And the timing is just adding insult to injury. It's an unfortunate situation for Manuel, but everyone has to deal with it privately as they see fit. But of course, what's happened in recent weeks is certainly not the best thing for Manuel's reputation.

    'He made that decision, but I think it wasn't the best time. On the other hand, he has to sort it out for himself, he has to try to solve his personal problems himself.

    Sources indicate that 'I also don't know what the agreement is between him and his wife. He's old enough and actually clever enough.

    Recent findings suggest that 'And from that perspective, it did surprise me that he was going on vacation or to rehab in Sicily and Brazil at this particular time. Those are his private matters, but he could have arranged it better in terms of timing.'.

    Neuer, who won 128 caps for Germany and was a key part of their 2014 World Cup winning squad, is at the moment sidelined with an ankle injury.

    Neuer, 40, is right now sidelined with an ankle injury and is expected to return in the New Year.

    Bayern Munich board member Max Eberl confirmed earlier this month that the veteran star had been given time off to relax, with his rehabilitation expected to see him return to action in the Upcoming Year.

    Sporting director Christoph Freund admitted on Thursday that Neuer is at the moment going through a ‘difficult period in his life’.

    Sources indicate that 'Manu is back [in Munich] now. He's obviously going through a difficult period in his life, particularly with this latest injury,’ Freund mentioned.

    Recent findings suggest that 'Manu naturally wants to spend as much time as possible with the team and be out on the pitch as much as possible. But I think this short period away, when he wasn't here every day in the rehab area, has done him quite a bit of good.

    According to recent reports, ‘He seems positive now. He wants to get back, the pain has subsided, and he's making good progress.

    ‘The other matters are Manu's private matters, and I don't want to comment on those. Of course, information spreads very swiftly these days.

    According to recent reports, ‘I think you always have to be very, very careful about what you associate yourself with when you don't know the exact circumstances. I know that's a rather general statement, but I think it's important to be extremely cautious.’.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Arsenal forward Kai Havertz is among the players to have received two yellow cards in this season's Champions League.

    Players will receive a one-match ban should they receive four yellow cards before the semi-finals of the Champions League.

    This rule runs from the start of the league phase until the end of the quarter-finals. After then, all yellow cards are wiped out and players cannot be suspended for multiple yellow cards.

    Yellow cards that result in a red card during a match do not count towards a player's tally, as a separate suspension will be served.

    The same rules apply for both the Europa League and the Conference League.

    During the opening three rounds of the Champions League, 16 players received two yellow cards, meaning they are now two cautions away from a one-match ban.

    There are now seven players on three yellow cards, putting them on the brink of a ban.

    It has been revealed that players can also be suspended if they pick up six, eight or 10 yellow cards. This would also result in a one-match suspension every time a player hits an even number of yellow cards above four.

    Red cards result in a one-match suspension, with Bayern Munich's Michael Olise missing his side's earlier clash with Arsenal after being sent off against Viking in the previous round of fixtures.

    Uefa may increase the length of a red card ban for serious offences such as violent conduct.

    Marlon Gomes (Shakhtar Donetsk).

    #164057. Germany's Early Start Pension: Can child investment accounts help?

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1022 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

    Germany's Early Start Pension: Can child investment accounts help?

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1022 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Germany's pension system is under growing strain as demographic change leaves a shrinking workforce funding the pensions of an increasing number of retirees.
    • Sources indicate that in the 1960s, for instance, six workers contributed to the pay-as-you-go public retirement system for each pensioner.
    • According to the Federal Statistical Office, Germany's fertility rate is right now 1.32 children per woman,and has remained below the 2.1 needed to maintain a stable population since the 1970s.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Germany's pension system is under growing strain as demographic change leaves a shrinking workforce funding the pensions of an increasing number of retirees.

    Sources indicate that in the 1960s, for instance, six workers contributed to the pay-as-you-go public retirement system for each pensioner. Today, that figure has fallen to just two contributors per retiree.

    According to the Federal Statistical Office, Germany's fertility rate is right now 1.32 children per woman,and has remained below the 2.1 needed to maintain a stable population since the 1970s.

    As a large cohort of baby boomers reaches retirement age, fewer young people are entering the workforce. Germany's working-age population is shrinking by around 1% each year due to demographic change alone, according to the German bank LBBW.

    To keep up, nearly a quarter of the federal budget, over €123 billion ($135 billion), is transferred to the statutory pension system each year to help finance pension payments.

    Now to help ease the pressure on the pension system, Chancellor Friedrich Merz's government plans to implement a raft of reforms, including a supplementary, capital-funded savings scheme known as the Frühstartrente, or Early Start Pension.

    Under the blueprint, the state would pay €10 per month into an investment account for every child and teenager aged six to 18.

    Beneficiaries would not be able to access the money until they reach retirement age, though current aims would allow the funds to be transferred into private retirement accounts. Investment returns would be tax-free during the accumulation phase and taxed only when funds are withdrawn.

    Assuming an average annual return of 7%, the €1,440 contributed by the government over 12 years would grow to around €53,000 by retirement, according to government projections.

    Parents and relatives would be able to make additional contributions. If they invest an extra €50 per month, the account could grow to as much as €300,000 by retirement.

    Starting to save early makes sense because of the power of compound interest, Axel Börsch-Supan, a professor of economics at the Technical University of Munich, told DW.

    "But it will not solve Germany's pension problems, which stem from the pay-as-you-go system and costly policies such as the pension level guarantee and retirement at 63," he added, referring to a provision that allows workers with at least 45 years of pension contributions to retire at age 63 with a full pension.

    To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

    Börsch-Supan argues that government subsidies under the program are likely to benefit higher-income families more than lower-income households.

    "That's a waste of taxpayer money, because higher-income individuals are already well-positioned to provide for their own retirement and that of their children," he stated.

    The Ifo Institute, one of Germany's leading economic think tanks, shares a similar assessment.

    It argues that the scheme effectively means "the government hands out money indiscriminately, only to reclaim it through taxes from the same citizens.".

    The government, however, argues that the proposal gives every child a head start in the capital markets regardless of their family's financial circumstances and helps them build retirement savings and long-term wealth.

    Similar capital market-based savings and investment accounts for children exist in several countries, including the United Kingdom, Israel, Canada and Singapore.

    Many of these programs include government contributions, matching payments or tax incentives designed to encourage long-term saving and asset accumulation from an early age.

    But Germany's plan differs slightly as it links state-funded childhood investment accounts directly to retirement provision.

    The government also hopes the program will boost financial literacy among children and young adults by familiarizing them with investing, saving and capital markets.

    To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

    Johannes Geyer, deputy head of the department of public economics at the German Institute for Economic Research (DIW Berlin), indicates there is little evidence the Early Start Pension will fundamentally change how people engage with financial markets.

    Recent findings suggest that "The idea is that people will develop a connection to the capital markets through their experiences with their investment portfolios," he told DW. "But this is not very convincing. We neither know what experiences the future will bring nor what conclusions people will draw from them.".

    Geyer stresses that the program's impact will not be visible for decades because participants cannot access the funds until retirement.

    "If we start now with the 2020 and 2021 cohorts, we're talking about the 2080s. That's a bit too far in the future to be able to draw meaningful conclusions.".

    In the meantime, he states, the scheme's most immediate effect may be to strengthen ties between families and financial institutions, particularly if account holders make additional contributions.

    Opposition parties, including the Greens and the Left Party, have criticized the strategy, arguing it would reinforce social disparities and boost inequality since better-off parents could pay more into accounts.

    Yet Geyer says the measure won't increase inequality per se. "Sure, wealthy families are more likely to top up their contributions more substantially. But they probably would have done that anyway," he underscored.

    "A more interesting question is whether the measure can also encourage people with limited financial means to invest in stocks," he mentioned.

    Geyer points out that Germany cannot entirely escape the costs of demographic decline and an aging society.

    To address the challenge, he calls for a moderate increase in pension contributions, a broader contributor base that includes groups such as the self-employed, and policies aimed at attracting more qualified workers to the labor market.

    Börsch-Supan, who specializes in the economics of aging, says the government's primary goal should be to stabilize the pay-as-you-go statutory pension system.

    "A transition to a fully funded pension system would actually be desirable, but it would initially place a heavy double burden on the younger generation, because they would have to save for themselves while also paying contributions for their parents," he explained.

    The expert also suggests other measures like restoring the sustainability factor, which is designed to link annual pension hikes to demographic shifts, and linking the retirement age to life expectancy.

    💡 Key Takeaways

    • At 11:51am on Sunday morning, the news everyone expected had arrived and Alessio Dionisi was relieved of his duties as Watford head coach after five months in charge, following a dismal 4-0 away defeat to Sheffield United, which left the club just one place above the relegation zone.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Some things are certain in life; death, taxes and Watford sacking another head coach.

    At 11:51am on Sunday morning, the news everyone expected had arrived and Alessio Dionisi was relieved of his duties as Watford head coach after five months in charge, following a dismal 4-0 away defeat to Sheffield United, which left the club just one place above the relegation zone.

    It was the latest in a series of lifeless performances from a Watford side that have looked ill-equipped for Championship football from the moment the season started.

    Now, at a time where Watford need Championship experience more than ever, owner Gino Pozzo has turned to former Romania boss Edward Iordanescu, a man that has had 13 jobs in 15 years, never managed more than 60 games at any team and most importantly, never played or coached in England or in one of Europe’s major leagues.

    Given Watford’s reputation with head coaches, many would joke Iordanescu’s appointment sounds like a match made in heaven.

    For Hornets fans, though, it’s an act of desperation from a club that has no initiative, structure or hope.

    In truth, Dionisi is the latest in a series of head coaches who have been let down by owner Pozzo, chairman Scott Duxbury and technical director Gianluca Nani, who seem incapable of building a squad or supporting a head coach.

    The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

    According to recent reports, things could have been so different for the Italian, because at the start of the season, there was clearly something there. Watford were excellent in their opening day win over Southampton - playing with real flair and intensity in the first half - and followed that up with draws against Wrexham and West Ham. It was clear the players respected the Italian.

    However, the warning signs were already there. In the summer, Dionisi and supporters were told that Watford would prioritise experienced players in the transfer market. None arrived.

    Nestory Irankunda, Imran Louza and Giorgi Chakvetadze - three key players - were sold and not replaced, with Watford starting the season with just two centre-backs on the club’s books and two fit central midfielders.

    The Italian sounded increasingly exasperated as his calls for reinforcements fell on deaf ears until the final few days of the window, where Watford eventually panicked and brought in Stephy Mavididi, Soumaila Coulibaly and Branimir Mlacic on loan. Myron Boadu and Michail Antonio arrived on free transfers.

    Most of those players arrived unfit and come September, Dionisi was struggling to fill the bench as injuries took hold. The Italian never really recovered from embarrassing defeats to Burnley and Cardiff City, deploying a back five in recent weeks as he attempted to make the Golden Boys harder to beat.

    Recent findings suggest that quite frankly, Watford are unmanageable. Not even Pep Guardiola would be successful at Vicarage Road, because no head coach is given the opportunity to implement a style of play when they have to contend with poor recruitment, a leadership vacuum and a dressing room with seemingly poor attitudes.

    It has been revealed that rob Edwards was promised he'd be backed in the transfer market come hell or high water by chairman Duxbury in the summer of 2022. Most of the signings he received didn't fit his system and he was sacked within two months of the season starting.

    After Edwards, Slaven Bilic thought he'd be able to sign players he wanted in the January transfer window. He received Joao Ferreira and Henrique Araujo - both of whom never looked suited to Championship football – as well as Ryan Porteous, Wesley Hoedt and Britt Assombalonga. Bilic was gone by March.

    Then came Chris Wilder, who repeatedly called out the poor attitude within the dressing room and wasn't given a contract extension when his deal expired in the summer of 2023. After the wheels came off under Valerian Ismael, Tom Cleverley was promoted to head coach in 2024 and despite a thin squad, united the players and fans, having been a popular player at Vicarage Road during his playing days.

    Once again, though, January arrived and Cleverley didn't get the options he so dearly needed, meaning Watford's form dropped off and he was sacked, somewhat harshly, at the end of the season.

    Just last season, the popular Javi Gracia returned for a second spell in charge and had Watford in the play-off spots by January. He was promised additions, but none were forthcoming and ultimately the Spaniard decided the job wasn't worth his time. Gracia resigned, returning to Spain to spend time with his family.

    Recent findings suggest that in short, it's time the Watford ownership took a long, hard look at themselves, rather than the head coach. Has Iordanescu been appointed because no one sensible will take it? Any head coach worth his salt in England - and possibly now Italy, too - knows what they’re walking into.

    In a recent interview with Roy Moore from the 1881 Movement, Pozzo tried shifting accountability for the club’s downfall, which can be traced back to the FA Cup Final in 2019. Since then, numerous decisions have, in the eyes of supporters, led to the erosion of the club's identity - fans have had enough.

    Empty statements, the constant churn of players and head coaches, and what appears to be a lack of any real structure or plan - supporters are fed up.

    The fact Watford closed their Under-21 setup, downgraded their academy and sold off the women's team this summer was a huge source of disappointment for fans, too, given the club’s rich history of bringing players through their youth system.

    Unless there is a sudden change of approach overnight, Watford are only heading one way and that's down to League 1.

    Bradley is a sports journalist and Watford fan, who previously spent seven years working for talkSPORT. During his time with the station, he covered the Premier League, EFL and WSL, as well as the Lionesses, and interviewed the likes of Pep Guardiola, Ange Postecoglou, Mikel Arteta, Sarina Wiegman, Alessia Russo, Hannah Hampton and Oscar among others. In his spare time, he is the commentator for Non League side Harefield United. Previously, he worked for Newsquest, covering both Watford and Leyton Orient for the Watford Observer and East London Guardian Series newspapers. He has also had pieces published in the Daily Mail and Watford's matchday programme.
