    #163979. 'I've lost her forever' — Why German voice actors are refusing to sign Netflix's AI contract

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (954 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

    'I've lost her forever' — Why German voice actors are refusing to sign Netflix's AI contract

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (954 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • When does Cameron Diaz not sound like Cameron Diaz?
    • For more than 30 years, whenever the Oscar-winning actor has appeared on German screens, she has spoken with the voice of Katrin Fröhlich.
    • It has been revealed that the same goes for all other famous actors.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    When does Cameron Diaz not sound like Cameron Diaz? When you're in a German cinema.

    For more than 30 years, whenever the Oscar-winning actor has appeared on German screens, she has spoken with the voice of Katrin Fröhlich.

    It has been revealed that the same goes for all other famous actors. In Germany's €125-million ($138-million) voiceover industry, Hollywood's up-and-comers are "adopted" by a voice actor who provides their German voice — often for decades — ensuring continuity and a certain relationship to the stars for audiences.

    But on Netflix, and perhaps elsewhere, many of those voices might be about to change.

    Recently, Fröhlich and fellow voice actors Anne Helm (Margot Robbie) and Luise Helm (Scarlett Johansson) published a video on social media, letting their followers know they wouldn't provide their voices anymore.

    The reason? They refuse to sign Netflix's contract, seen by DW, which contains a clause that lets the American entertainment giant use their voices for training its AI.

    They're not the first voiceover artists to speak out on the topic. But they are the first ones to go viral.

    According to recent reports, "It was unexpected, completely," Fröhlich said. "For whatever reason, we managed to reach people, perhaps because … we are three well-known women in the voiceover industry.".

    "Over the years, we've managed to make good names for ourselves. It seems to have touched people that we made this statement together," she said.

    The new AI clause has been in Netflix's contracts since January 2026. Voice actors sign one ahead of every production. It was negotiated by BFFS, Germany's union for film and television actors.

    According to recent reports, fröhlich, like a significant number of voice actors, is not a member and feels as though the union went over their heads. However, BFFS claims the deal gives them protection they wouldn't otherwise have.

    Till Völger, an attorney and member of the union's board, claims previous contracts and those with other streaming services are silent on AI or contain sweeping AI permissions.

    If an AI-generated voice doesn't sound like a particular person, companies are free to use the data they have gathered as they wish. Training can take place in other jurisdictions and may not require the actor's consent at all, he pointed out.

    "We have a massive, massive protection gap," Völger told DW.

    To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

    According to recent reports, against that backdrop, BFFS argues the deal with Netflix is a step forward. It allows the company to train its own systems with recordings, but voice actors must give separate, explicit consent before their recordings are used to create actual AI-generated voices, even if the voice isn't recognizable as theirs.

    Sources indicate that "We've created a contractual right that the law doesn't provide," said Völger. "Is the situation perfect? No. Is it better than before? Yes.".

    Recent findings suggest that he would like to see other streaming services agree to the same conditions that Netflix has. In his view, only legislation could create the necessary protections voice actors are seeking.

    Netflix says human performance "is and remains notable to us," in statement provided to DW.

    "In recent years, we have commissioned thousands of hours of German dubbing, and we intend to continue supporting a similar volume of work and the use of human voices," the statement continued.

    Matti Klemm, the voice of Jason Momoa and beloved children's cartoon elephant Benjamin Blümchen, sees things differently. Like Fröhlich, he is refusing to sign the latest contract.

    According to recent reports, "In short, it says: as soon as I record something for Netflix, I'm automatically training their AI, for free," he told DW. "My job is to create a German original, a dubbed version with my performance, not to train the computer systems of some tech companies.".

    He is taking Netflix to court, backed by the Society for Civil Rights (GFF), to find out how his voice has been used for training in previous projects.

    According to Davy Wang, who is coordinating the case for Klemm and GFF, the lawsuit will seek to stop Netflix using his recordings for training, disclose how previous data was used and establish whether Klemm is entitled to any damages.

    The suit will be filed at the end of the year or in early 2027. Supporters donated more than €50,000 to the legal fund in the first week following its announcement.

    For Klemm, what is at stake goes beyond training. "It's not about our voice, it's about our soul, our performance, the way we are," he said. "How far have we come when AI training matters more than my actual work?".

    Netflix remarked it cannot comment on a case that has not yet been filed.

    For a multimillion-euro industry, the outcome of the case could reach well beyond Netflix and other companies and creative branches are watching. But no matter what the outcome of the lawsuit or contract agreements, voice actors' fears for their future run deep.

    Those who don't sign contracts can't work, and streaming companies can make up a significant part of their income.

    "Many say: I've held out for 10 months, but I can't anymore. I have to sign this contract, I have to pay my rent, I have to feed my children," explained Fröhlich.

    Beyond that, many fear the future of their industry and the connections they have formed with stars and audiences.

    "For a many people I'm connected with Cameron Diaz and I evoke something within them," said Fröhlich.

    Recent findings suggest that but if Diaz is involved in more Netflix projects, "then I've basically lost her," she concluded. "I'll never be her voice again.".

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (643 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later?
    • The Europa League game between Besiktas and Israel's Hapoel Beer-Sheva was suspended for around 30 minutes on Thursday when police clashed with fans of the Turkish club after they displayed a banner in support of Palestine.
    • The game, being played on neutral ground in Batumi, Georgia, was halted in the 26th minute but restarted after the interruption.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

    The Europa League game between Besiktas and Israel's Hapoel Beer-Sheva was suspended for around 30 minutes on Thursday when police clashed with fans of the Turkish club after they displayed a banner in support of Palestine.

    The game, being played on neutral ground in Batumi, Georgia, was halted in the 26th minute but restarted after the interruption.

    Turkey’s Haberturk broadcaster stated Georgian police used pepper spray against the Besiktas fans, who also unfurled a Palestinian flag, prompting referee referee Morten Krogh to stop the game with the score 0-0.

    Besiktas went on to win the game 2-1.

    In a statement, Besiktas accused the Georgian security forces of using “disproportionate” force against supporters before and during the game.

    Georgian police entered the stands and ⁠used pepper spray on Besiktas fans, Turkish outlet NTV reported.

    “We strongly condemn the security forces for their use of disproportionate force against our fans,” the club said. “We also extend our best wishes for a speedy recovery to all our fans affected by these incidents.”.

    The report added that Turkish fans chanted “Down with Israel” and that Besiktas players and director of football Onder Ozen spoke to supporters before play restarted to calm the situation.

    It has been revealed that the Turkish Football Federation condemned the treatment of Besiktas supporters on X, saying they were subjected to unacceptable behaviour and discrimination. It said it would press for an investigation.

    The TFF’s statement read: “We strongly condemn the unacceptable attitudes, conduct and interference directed at Beşiktaş supporters, both inside and outside the stadium, before and during our club’s Uefa Europa League match against Hapoel Beer-Sheva in Georgia.

    “No practice that disregards the universal values of sport, human dignity, mutual respect and the principles of fair play, or that involves discrimination, exclusion or security failures, can be tolerated.

    “Nor can there be any question of remaining silent in the face of such conduct, which endangers our supporters’ safety and targets their fundamental rights and freedoms.

    “As the Turkish Football Federation, we declare unequivocally that we will follow this matter to its conclusion to ensure that the events are fully investigated, those responsible are identified and the necessary sanctions are imposed without delay.

    “There must be no tolerance for covering up these events, allowing those responsible to evade accountability or permitting similar violations to recur.

    “We emphasize that we stand firmly with our club, Besiktas, and our supporters, who faced a series of problems, particularly serious security failures, and extend our best wishes for a speedy recovery to all our supporters subjected to interference and mistreatment.

    “Let no one forget that we will not remain silent in the face of disrespect, discrimination and security violations directed at representatives and supporters of Turkish football.

    “We will act decisively on national and international platforms to ensure that all necessary steps are taken, particularly with Uefa, and that those responsible are held accountable.”.

    Turkish clubs echoed the sentiments of the TFF, with Besiktas’ rivals Fenerbahce, Galatasaray and Trabzonspor all among those to stand with the club.

    “We do not accept Turkish clubs being denied the right to play their home matches in their own country, in front of their own fans, when facing clubs from the occupying state of Israel,” Trabzonspor wrote in a statement.

    Sources indicate that “We do not consider Uefa’s double standards on this matter acceptable. We also strongly condemn the disproportionate intervention by security forces against Besiktas fans in Georgia this evening.”.

    The ⁠officiating team and the Besiktas players ‌left ​the pitch before ‌the game restarted.

    Earlier, the Besiktas players refused to shake hands with their Hapoel counterparts, the state-run Anadolu Agency reported.

    Hapoel Beer-Sheva and Israel FA had not commented on the incident at the time of publishing.

    Newcastle United star Sven Botman has been banned from driving after he was caught using his mobile phone at the wheel.

    The Ministry of Justice (MoJ) confirmed that Botman, 26, pleaded guilty at Newcastle Magistrates Court on Wednesday.

    The Dutch international defender was given six penalty points and disqualified from driving for six months, as these were added to points he had already accrued.

    The MoJ said Botman was fined £900 and ordered to pay £400 costs and a £360 surcharge.

    Court documents show that Botman was in a Land Rover on the A189 Haddricks Mill Road, in Newcastle, on 17 September when he was spotted using his phone.

    According to The Sun, the court heard he was filmed by a cyclist while he was stationary in traffic.

    The Dutch centre-half was signed by Newcastle in a £32 million deal from French club Lille during the summer of 2022.

    Since signing for the Magpies, Botman has made 124 appearances and was part of the squad that won the League Cup in 2025, their first major trophy in decades.

    Bruno Fernandes is STAYING at Man United - for now! Red Devils trigger 12-month extension clause to prevent losing captain for free - as he weighs up long-term deal

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Published: 09:49 EST, 27 November 2026 | Updated: 11:55 EST, 27 November 2026.
    • Manchester United have triggered the 12-month extension clause in Bruno Fernandes' contract after their captain put talks over a upcoming deal on hold.
    • The move means Fernandes is tied to Old Trafford until June 30, 2028, and will not be able to negotiate with foreign clubs from January 1 or leave United as a free agent in the summer.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

    Published: 09:49 EST, 27 November 2026 | Updated: 11:55 EST, 27 November 2026.

    Manchester United have triggered the 12-month extension clause in Bruno Fernandes' contract after their captain put talks over a upcoming deal on hold.

    The move means Fernandes is tied to Old Trafford until June 30, 2028, and will not be able to negotiate with foreign clubs from January 1 or leave United as a free agent in the summer.

    The Portugal star could still be sold at the end of the season, but having him under contract for an additional 12 months means United are guaranteed to receive a transfer fee.

    It's understood that United and Fernandes aim to return to the negotiating table in future, but have decided that it is more key to focus on lifting the team away from the Premier League relegation zone.

    Fernandes, who moved to Old Trafford from Sporting Lisbon in January 2020 in a deal worth up to £68million, spoke about the situation when he returned to his old club for Wednesday's 2-2 Champions League draw at the Jose Alvalade Stadium.

    Sources indicate that 'There are no negotiations going on,' he said. 'Yes, the club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, indicates that they want me to stay.

    Manchester United have triggered the 12-month extension clause in Bruno Fernandes' contract.

    The Red Devils captain is an notable figure in the dressing room for Mauricio Pochettino.

    Fernandes scored the first goal of Pochettino's reign from the penalty spot against Sporting.

    'I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations. We spoke about the contract at the end of last season, we came in the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side.

    'I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations because the most crucial thing now is that the club gets back to win games.'.

    Fernandes came close to a £100m transfer to Saudi Pro League side Al Hilal in 2025, and was again linked with a move away from United in the summer after setting a new Premier League record for assists last season.

    He has struggled by comparison this term and was dropped for the defeat to Bournemouth at Old Trafford last month, but returned to form with two goals and a man-of-the-match performance against Sporting.

    However, Fernandes is a doubt for Saturday's home game against Brentford after missing training on Friday through illness following United's return from Portugal.

    According to recent reports, 'We don't know,' remarked head coach Mauricio Pochettino. 'He's affected for a virus from Portugal. He finished the game a little bit with a problem and today he cannot be part of the training session.

    'We are going to assess during the day and tomorrow how is how. We wake up and see. We are not going to take any risks with this type of situation. We are going to pay attention.'.

    Pochettino revealed that £70m summer signing Carlos Baleba could be out for up to another nine weeks with the hamstring injury he suffered against Roma earlier this month.

    Baleba has already been sidelined for three weeks, and Pochettino mentioned: 'The medical staff say they were talking about 10-12 weeks.'.

    Marcus Rashford, who has been following an individual fitness programme for a hip and groin problem, has returned to light training on the grass at Carrington.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Tottenham Hotspur’s resurgence under Roberto De Zerbi has breathed fresh life into the club after back-to-back 17th-placed finishes.
    • There is one clear deficiency in their current make-up that threatens to limit what they can achieve in 2026/27, though - they can't finish.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tottenham Hotspur’s resurgence under Roberto De Zerbi has breathed fresh life into the club after back-to-back 17th-placed finishes.

    There is one clear deficiency in their current make-up that threatens to limit what they can achieve in 2026/27, though - they can't finish.

    Despite sitting comfortably in the top half after 12 games, Spurs’ underlying attacking numbers tell the story of a side creating plenty and squandering too much of it.

    Tottenham have rattled off 170 shots in the Premier League this season - the fifth-highest tally in the division - while only Liverpool and Manchester City have registered more efforts from inside the penalty area than Spurs’ 109.

    But, when it comes to actually hitting the target, De Zerbi’s side slump to 14th across the top flight.

    According to recent reports, there's also an issue with their ball-striking. According to Gradient Sports’ analysts, just six of Spurs’ 170 league attempts have been graded as ‘unsaveable’ - a figure bettered by every team in the Premier League bar Everton (5).

    According to recent reports, for context, high-flying Brighton have racked up 20 unsaveable efforts, while Erling Haaland has managed seven on his own. At 3.5 per cent, Tottenham boast the lowest proportion of unsaveable shots in the entire division.

    The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

    A glance at De Zerbi’s attacking options explains why to some extent. Richarlison has been frozen out entirely and is angling for a January move, Dominic Solanke has managed just two league goals, and substantial-money summer arrival Omar Marmoush is yet to hit the ground running in north London.

    Centre-back Jan Paul van Hecke is the team's joint-top Premier League goalscorer with two goals after 12 matches: Spurs need a centre-forward in January.

    Enter Real Sociedad’s 22-year-old Icelandic international Orri Oskarsson.

    Oskarsson is by no means LaLiga’s most prolific frontman, having netted four times in the Spanish top flight this term but his underlying metrics point towards a striker ready to thrive in a possession-heavy, attack-minded system.

    Unlike De Zerbi’s Spurs, Real Sociedad do not dominate the ball as often, leaving their striker without service for large periods of matches. Oskarsson, though, is making every second count when his team are in possession, averaging a goal every 64 minutes that La Real actually have the ball this season.

    In total, he has scored nine times across his last 13 appearances for club and country.

    What makes Oskarsson particularly suited to Tottenham is how intelligently he moves to receive the ball. Gradient Sports’ data indicates the Icelandic forward receives line-breaking passes 45 per cent of the time, placing him among LaLiga’s best at peeling off defenders and making himself available to creative midfielders.

    That off-the-ball awareness is reinforced by the fact he has received the ball in a clear shooting position 10 times in the league this season - a tally bettered only by Barcelona’s Raphinha (13) and Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe (11).

    Recent findings suggest that once the ball arrives at his feet, Oskarsson has the penalty-box nous Tottenham lack. Ninety-two per cent of his LaLiga shots this season have been taken from inside the box, which aligns nicely with the 109 close-range openings Spurs have already generated this term. Even more impressive, out of the 25 shots he has taken in LaLiga, five have been graded as unsaveable by Gradient's analysts - just one fewer than Tottenham’s entire squad combined.

    Gradient have also flagged just one occasion all season where Oskarsson opted to shoot when passing to a better-placed teammate was the superior option, highlighting good judgement under pressure and decision-making that is rare for a 22-year-old.

    Meanwhile, his Expected Goals (xG) ranks sixth-highest in LaLiga - a decent return given Real Sociedad’s modest share of possession and chance creation.

    Recent findings suggest that and best of all, a winter deal is entirely plausible. For a Tottenham side creating plenty of penalty-box opportunities but with nobody reliable to tuck them away, Oskarsson could be one of the more shrewd January investments the market has to offer.

Joe takes a keen interest in youth football, covering PL2, U21 Euros, as well as U20 and U17 World Cups in the past, in addition to hosting the industry-leading football recruitment-focused SCOUTED podcast. He is also one of the lucky few to have 'hit top bins' as a contestant on Soccer AM. It wasn't a shin-roller.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

    Lionel Messi will play his first match in Argentina since his international retirement when he takes part in Carlos Tevez’s testimonial in December.

    Messi called time on his 21-year career with La Albiceleste in October, scoring his 126th and final Argentina goal in a 3-0 friendly win over Benin.

    It was an emotional send-off for a player that is deified in his homeland, but Argentinians haven’t had to wait long for Messi to come back, with the 39-year-old confirming his next footballing commitment in the country.

    The Inter Miami superstar will feature in the testimonial match of his former international team-mate Tevez, which is being held at Boca Juniors’ iconic stadium La Bombonera.

    Tevez saw out his career at boyhood club Boca Juniors in 2022, bringing down the curtain on a career that included spells at Manchester City, Manchester United and Juventus.

    Tevez made 76 caps and scored 13 times for Argentina, winning an Olympic gold medal with his country at the 2004 Games.

    Nicknamed “Apache”, 42-year-old Tevez said last year he wanted Messi and former United team-mate Cristiano Ronaldo to play on opposing teams in his testimonial.

    And while Ronaldo will not be involved barring a dramatic late addition, Messi will turn out for a man he shared the international stage with for a decade.

    "It will be a ⁠true honour to welcome the best player in the world to Apache’s last dance," organisers posted on Instagram on Thursday.

    Other stars involved in Tevez’s testimonial includes ex-United team-mate Rio Ferdinand, former City strike-partner Sergio Aguero and goalkeeper Gianluigi Buffon, who was Tevez’s captain at Juventus.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Panini have launched their latest Barclays Women's Super League sticker collection, featuring teams from WSL and WSL 2 for a second year running.
    • This is only the fourth edition of the book for the top women’s league in this country, and Rachel Daly believes the culture of sticker collecting can play its part in growing the women’s game.
    • As the latest collection was released in London this week, the ex-Lioness spoke to FourFourTwo about the rise of the women's game.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Panini have launched their latest Barclays Women's Super League sticker collection, featuring teams from WSL and WSL 2 for a second year running.

    This is only the fourth edition of the book for the top women’s league in this country, and Rachel Daly believes the culture of sticker collecting can play its part in growing the women’s game.

    As the latest collection was released in London this week, the ex-Lioness spoke to FourFourTwo about the rise of the women's game.

    Speaking at the launch, Daly reflected on her own childhood memories of collecting Panini stickers.

    Recent findings suggest that "For me, it goes back to my childhood,” Daly told FourFourTwo. “I collected them with my brother. We used to, every Saturday morning, go and get the stickers.

    Sources indicate that "You'd get your piles and you'd trade them and swap them at school. Just that whole feeling of sitting down and putting stickers in.

    "So to be in one is pretty cool.

    The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

    "I'm a Leeds fan, so I always wanted to get the whole Leeds team immediately when I was younger.

    "I would literally swap any of my stickers, even if I'd already got the Leeds player, just to have more.”.

    While Daly grew up collecting men’s players, this WSL collection offers an opportunity to introduce more fans to the women's game, something Daly believes is particularly key as the league continues to grow.

    The latest album has 545 stickers across all 26 WSL and WSL2 clubs, giving fans access to collect stickers of their favourite players from across the top two tiers of English women’s football.

    "The visibility of the game is massive," she added.

    According to recent reports, "For the fact that it's WSL 1 and 2, I think it's equally as vital. Those players in the WSL 2 deserve the same recognition as us.

    "Being able to see kids being exposed to seeing the women's game as well, it's exciting.".

    Daly was speaking at the launch of the Panini Barclays Women's Super League Official Sticker Collection 2027 in London. The collection is available now at retailers nationwide and online via Panini.co.uk.

    Breaking: Daily briefing: A guide to the Riemann hypothesis

    📅 28 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1269 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, an analysis of protein-coding DNA from more than 1.4 million people has identified hundreds of genes that influence a person’s height.
    • It has been revealed that the number of reported global cases of the viral disease dengue in 2024 — a 34-fold increase from the 430,000 reported in 1990.
    • Reference: Research Square preprint (not peer reviewed).
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, an analysis of protein-coding DNA from more than 1.4 million people has identified hundreds of genes that influence a person’s height. Researchers identified 207 genes that were linked to a height difference of two centimetres, on average. They also identified 17 rare variants that prevent proteins from functioning, which have more striking effects. These include one variant associated with a 17-centimetre reduction in height and another with an 11-centimetre increase. The findings might help with the development of treatments that mitigate height changes caused by some medical conditions.

    It has been revealed that the number of reported global cases of the viral disease dengue in 2024 — a 34-fold increase from the 430,000 reported in 1990. (Nature | 5 min read).

    Reference: Research Square preprint (not peer reviewed).

    Recent findings suggest that major prizes in economics, including the Nobel, are being awarded to researchers affiliated to an increasingly concentrated set of US universities. Just eight institutions dominate these top economics awards: Harvard University; the University of Chicago; Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT); Stanford University; Princeton University; Yale University; the University of California, Berkeley; and Columbia University. On the other hand, prizes in the natural sciences, engineering and social sciences outside economics have become less concentrated to certain institutions over the past 70 years.

    Reference: National Bureau of Economic Research working paper (not peer reviewed).

    Recent findings suggest that four years after NASA’s DART Earth-defence test mission smashed into an asteroid and succeeded in altering the space rock’s movement, a follow-up mission has confirmed it on camera. The European Space Agency has released the first images from its Hera mission, which show detailed views of the asteroid’s newly introduced crater. “Hera is a sort of Inspector Columbo going back to the crash scene to investigate what is the outcome of this impact,” indicates Patrick Michel, principal investigator of the Hera mission.

    The Newly introduced York Times | 7 min read.

    It has been revealed that this clip indicates the final five-and-a-half minutes of images leading up to the DART spacecraft's intentional collision with asteroid Dimorphos. This replay movie is 10 times faster than reality, except for the last six images, which are shown at the same rate that the spacecraft returned them. (NASA/Johns Hopkins APL).

    In a recent development, last week, the field of mathematics was rocked by two competing announcements about solving the Riemann hypothesis. The hypothesis is considered one of the most important open problems in maths. But if, like me, you have some trouble getting to grips with the famed conjecture — and what solving it could actually mean — Nature has you covered.

    Recent findings suggest that the hypothesis concerns the distribution of primes, and it is vital because these numbers are central to all of maths. Riemann arrived at his idea by studying prime numbers as waves and, at its heart, it boils down to a statistical test. One that will be familiar to any scientist who’s ever analysed data.

    According to recent reports, “If we can solve Riemann, what can’t we do?” claims Xin Zhang, one of five mathematicians who spoke to Nature in the aftermath of the proofs’ publication. His reaction was one of excitement, despite Anthropic’s use of artificial-intelligence to develop its proof. But his enthusiasm was by no means universal. The format of Anthropic’s proof — 17 million lines of code with no natural-language version for humans to work with — is “the worst-case scenario”, says Álvaro Lozano-Robledo. And the shift towards AI-use in maths is “a choice to disempower ourselves”, says Tasmin Chu.

    Bashyal observes a species of Coelogyne orchid, often found in tropical lowland forests and mountainous regions.Credit: CJ Karki for Nature.

    It has been revealed that wildlife conservationist Reshu Bashyal works with people in Nepal to protect the more than 500 species of orchids that grow there. Prized for their ornamental value and uses in traditional medicine, hundreds of these flowering plants are illegally harvested and sold each year. But blanket bans on the orchid trade are unlikely to be effective, Bashyal says, so more innovative strategies are required. One of these is an ‘anti-poaching taskforce’ that can document illegal activity, conduct patrols and spread information about the importance of conservation. (Nature | Leisurely scroll).

    A biomedical innovation model that utilizes scientists in industry with government as their main funder could accelerate the development of therapeutics for common diseases that industry considers too risky to invest in, argue physician Victor Dzau, health-policy advisor Emily Shambaugh and healthcare entrepreneur Will Ellaissi. This government funding could operate at a national level, or several countries could form a consortium. Such a model “moves beyond the market-determined trajectory of research translation and ensures the public’s role in shaping the future of health,” the authors write.

    It has been revealed that commensality — the act of sitting down to eat a meal with other people — has myriad health and social benefits, such as protecting against cognitive decline and helping us build trust with others. The presence of other people might also increase the enjoyment we get from eating. In an increasingly digital world, it might seem that opportunities to dine with others are dwindling. But research suggests that people are much more open and willing to accept invitations than we think, and simply putting ourselves out there might be an easy way to a dinner date.

    Recent findings suggest that evolutionary biologist Pamela Yeh shares advice on how to navigate grief in the demanding environment of academia. (Nature | 8 min read).

    doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03894-3.

    Today I’m appreciating the world in monochrome through the entries into this year’s Black and White Photo Awards. The overall winner, photographer Shengwai Dai’s Bishwa Ijtema, depicts a man’s leap of faith between the tops of two train cars — “a scene filled with energy, tension, and detail”, the competition’s judges said.

    Let me know which snap is your winner, along with any feedback on this newsletter, at briefing@nature.com.

    Jacob Smith, associate editor, Nature Briefing.

    German police respond to multiple school bomb threats

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (325 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dw

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Police in several locations across Germany reported large numbers of bomb threats targeting schools.
    • They said that while they were investigating the claims, they did not initially have reason to treat them as credible threats.
    • More than 400 schools in the southwestern state of Baden Württemberg received threats, and more than 250 in Saxony-Anhalt received the emails, with several other regions also targeted on Monday morning.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Police in several locations across Germany reported large numbers of bomb threats targeting schools.

    They said that while they were investigating the claims, they did not initially have reason to treat them as credible threats.

    More than 400 schools in the southwestern state of Baden Württemberg received threats, and more than 250 in Saxony-Anhalt received the emails, with several other regions also targeted on Monday morning.

    Police in Erfurt in Thuringia were among the first to issue a statement on the threats, saying they were responding to threats at "multiple schools" after morning warnings, including in Jena, Erfurt, Mühlhausen, Zella-Mehlis, Nordhausen, Gotha, Rudolstadt and Greiz.

    "The same word-for-word threats were received this morning at the various eductional institutes," police wrote in a press release. "Based on preliminary findings other federal states are also affected by the threatening messages.".

    In a recent development, police said they had no information yet on the potential author or sender of the emails. They were investigating breach of the peace-based crimes via the threat of criminal activity.

    "At present the police is not working on the assumption of the bomb threats being serious and recommends that schools do not implement evacuation measures and continue their normal operations," they remarked.

    Police in Freiburg in the southwest and authorities to the north in Hanover also remarked they were responding to emailed bomb threats directed against schools.

    Similar reports are emerging to the north of Germany in Denmark.

    As in Germany, Danish police remarked they did not believe the threats were credible, "but they understandably create insecurity locally at the schools.".

    This follows other recent cases of coordinated bomb threats against multiple schools that turned out to be hoaxes in Italy earlier in the month.

    It also comes amid various apparent bids to create disruption within Europe in recent weeks, such as multiple bomb threats targeting commercial airlines, or hacking into supermarket refrigeration systems to spoil produce en masse.

    Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca has downplayed concerns about his team’s togetherness and insisted he is not worried about star striker Erling Haaland following downcast post-match interviews.

    City had won 11 of their first 12 matches in all competitions this season but have suffered an alarming downturn in form, only winning two of their last seven games.

    Talisman Haaland has also suffered a slump at the same time, scoring just one goal in five games, and cut a morose figure when he was interviewed after a battling 2-2 draw against Napoli in the Champions League on Tuesday.

    However, Maresca has insisted their poor run and the Norwegian’s demeanour are not cause for concern.

    He noted: “I think Erling is a winner. It's normal that he's not happy when we don't win games but not just Erling, everyone.

    “Remember just a few weeks ago he was dancing inside the pitch. You can write and think many different things.

    According to recent reports, “Erling is upset. I'm upset because we're not winning games. But this is our job, this is football. That's why I need to maintain the balance.

    “He's a nine. They live day by day for goals and winning games. If they don't score or win games they're upset. So I don't think that affects his game but for sure he's not happy not winning games, but everyone is on the same page.”.

    Asked whether it has been business as usual in training, he said: “He has been good. Yes, normal like since day one. Again, a few weeks ago he was dancing inside the pitch, he was dancing in training. He's happy. It's normal that results affect the mood, that's why we need to win games.

    “But I don't see any problem at all with Erling.”.

    It has been revealed that the Italian insisted that “transition takes time” and added: “For me, it's completely normal, I'm completely relaxed, no panic at all. I understand that we need to win games because it's our business but for me, it's all normal.”.

    Asked whether their string of poor results, which includes a 10-game run without a clean sheet, had affected players’ confidence, he mentioned: “For sure, when you don't win games, it's not the ideal situation. But we won games at the beginning. We have also seven or eight new players that need to be used to winning games, so it's just a process.”.

    City face another significant test as they visit league leaders Arsenal, who are six points ahead, on Sunday.

    It has been revealed that maresca was insistent that City were not lacking in belief ahead of their trip to the defending champions, saying: “I think we have already shown this season that we are able to win important games, to win away. I don't see any reason why we are not able to win there.”.

    By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

    Published: 10:49 EST, 27 November 2026 | Updated: 12:07 EST, 27 November 2026.

    Gary Neville has claimed he is 'absolutely certain' Erling Haaland will leave Manchester City for Real Madrid within the next 18 months amid the impact of their legal battle with the Premier League.

    Haaland has cut a despondent figure in recent weeks following Man City's underwhelming run of form.

    The Norwegian star admitted to 'questioning everything' after their 2-2 draw against Napoli in the Champions League in midweek, while Man City fans expressed concerns over Haaland's downbeat assessment and body language.

    The result meant City have won just twice in their last seven matches – one of which was achieved in a penalty shoot-out against Brighton in the Carabao Cup.

    Man City have suffered defeats to Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest in the Premier League in the run, as well as drawing with Fulham on the weekend.

    In a recent development, neville, speaking on the Overlap, suggested the mood at Man City may have been affected in recent weeks after the club were found guilty of the vast majority of charges brought against them by the Premier League for financial wrongdoing. Man City have since appealed the decision.

    Gary Neville has said he is 'absolutely certain' Erling Haaland will leave Manchester City for Real Madrid within the next 18 months.

    Neville suggested Haaland's spell at Man City could be coming to an end after questioning whether the 'cloud' of the Premier League charges verdict has impacted the mood at the club.

    The former Man United defender theorised that Haaland's time at the club could be coming to an end and that he expects the forward to join Real Madrid in the near future.

    'It feels like something has changed in these last few weeks with City, it feels like maybe that mood, that cloud, is just starting to [impact],' Neville noted.

    'I don't think Haaland is going to be here, I think he will be at Real Madrid in the next, maximum 18 months, maybe even at the end of the season.

    'I can see Vinicius leaving, I can see Mbappe going a bit to the left and Haaland going up there [down the middle].

    'If you look at Florentino Perez, he goes and signs the best strikers in the world, the best players in the world.

    'I just think because of what has happened to City, I think Haaland is going to Real Madrid.

    'I am absolutely certain he will be in a Real Madrid shirt in the next 18 months.'.

    It had long been viewed that Haaland's career initiative had involved moving to LaLiga, with Real Madrid long-term admirers.

    Real Madrid have held a long-standing interest in the Manchester City superstar.

    Neville claimed Real Madrid president Florentino Perez could opt to sell Vinicius Jr before moving for Haaland.

    The forward, however, signed a nine-and-a-half-year deal in early 2025, taking his Man City contract through to 2034.

    Haaland had pushed back against suggestions the case had affected their form during the international break, while stressing he was committed long-term to the club.

    The forward's first answer to Norwegian broadcaster TV2 had spanned two minutes and 14 seconds, as he reeled off the teams he had represented from 2009 to 2018, the years covered by the charges after he was asked about the club's situation.

    'In 2009, I played for Bryne U9s. In 2010, the U10s. In 2011, the U11s. 2012, the U12s, 2013, the U13s. Shall we continue? We don't need the whole list. 2014, the U14s. 2015, the U15s and the national team,' Haaland said.

    'Then the U16s, I think. In 2016, I moved up to Bryne's first team, second team and youth team. In 2017, I went to Molde. In 2018, I was with Molde. The first team, Molde 2 and a bit with the youth team.

    'So this is a question I struggle to answer because it's a legal battle….

    Sources indicate that 'It's a case between the Premier League and Manchester City that a panel will deal with. Am I supposed to answer that? I'm not really sure.'.

    Haaland cut a despondent figure in midweek as he admitted to 'questioning everything' after Man City's draw with Napoli continued their underwhelming form.

    Haaland has pushed back against suggestions the Premier League charges verdict has had an impact on Man City's form.

    He continued: 'It's a difficult question to answer when I don't really know that much about it.

    'I assume the answers will come… I don't know when. I haven't read much about it.

    'To be completely honest, I'm focused on trying to perform for Manchester City.'.

    Haaland, who has scored 176 goals in 214 appearances for Man City, will be hoping to spark Enzo Maresca's side back into form when they face Premier League leaders Arsenal on Sunday.

    Arsenal are presently six points clear of Man City heading into the match as they bid to retain their title this season.
